before.answer: Mankind is the special creation of God, made in God's own image as His highest creation. He created them male and female; each person was born a boy or a girl as a part of God's good plan. Our life purpose is to know God and enjoy Him forever.
before.right: In God's image, male and female, with purpose to know and enjoy God

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Genesis 1:31 says God saw all he made was very good, Genesis 2:16-17 gives man a command with a warning, and Romans 5:12 says sin entered through one man and death through sin.

before.question: Did God create people bad or good?
before.answer: In the beginning man was innocent of sin. God created man with freedom of choice. By his free choice man sinned against God and brought sin and death into the human race.
before.right: Created innocent with free choice, man sinned, bringing sin and death

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Genesis 3 records the serpent's temptation and the fall, Romans 5:12 says sin and death spread to all because all sinned, and Romans 5:19 says many were made sinners through one man's disobedience. Children's early sin and the temptation-filled world are only implied.

before.question: Why is there so much sin in the world today?
before.answer: After the temptation of Satan, man fell from his original innocence. That's why everyone is born with a nature inclined toward sin and why we live in an environment so full of temptation. It is also why children, as soon they are capable of making decisions about right and wrong, begin to break God's laws.
before.right: Man fell through Satan's temptation, so all are born inclined to sin

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Sin is lawlessness (1 John 3:4), anything not from faith (Romans 14:23), while God calls us to do all for His glory (1 Corinthians 10:31), and the wages of sin is death (Romans 6:23).

before.question: What is sin?
before.answer: Sin is anything a person thinks, says, or does that is contrary to how God tells us to live. Anything that is not done as an act of faith or for the glory of God is sin. Every sin deserves God's punishment.
before.right: Contrary to God's will or not done as faith for God's glory

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Psalm 8:5 says God crowned man with glory and honor. Genesis 1:27 says God made man in His image, and Romans 5:8 says Christ died for us while we were still sinners.

before.question: Even though everyone offends God by their sins, does He still consider people to be of value?
before.answer: Every human being is greatly valued by God and every human life is sacred. We know this because God created man in His own image and because Christ died for people. Therefore, every person of every race should be respected and treated with Christian love.
before.right: Every human being is greatly valued by God; God created us in His image and Christ died for us

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Second Peter 1:21 says men spoke from God as the Holy Spirit carried them, and 2 Timothy 3:16 calls all Scripture God-breathed. "Without any errors" is drawn from these, not stated outright.

before.question: How did we get the Bible?
before.answer: The Holy Bible was written by men inspired by God. Therefore God is its author. The Bible is without any errors. So all Scripture is totally true and trustworthy.
before.right: Men inspired by God wrote the Bible, making God its author, without error and totally true

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: 1 John 4:10 says love consists not in our loving God but in His loving us and sending His Son; 1 John 4:19 says, "We love because He first loved us."

before.question: Do we have to earn God's love?

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Psalm 5:5 says God hates workers of iniquity, Colossians 3:6 says God's wrath comes on sin, Isaiah 59:2 says iniquities separate us from God, and Romans 5:16 says sin brings condemnation.

before.question: How has sin ruined our relationship with God?
before.answer: Because God is holy He hates sin. Because He is a God of justice He must punish those responsible for sin. Sin separates us from God and brings us under condemnation.
before.right: God's holiness hates sin, His justice punishes it, separating us under condemnation

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Ephesians 2:8-9 names grace and faith as the means of salvation, Ephesians 1:7 ties forgiveness to Christ's blood, and Romans 10:9 says confessing Jesus as Lord and believing brings salvation.

before.question: How does the Bible teach that a person is saved?
before.answer: Only the grace of God can bring man into fellowship with God. Salvation is possible because Jesus died on the cross and shed His own blood to obtain forgiveness of sins. Salvation is offered freely to all who accept Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior. There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ.
before.right: Salvation is only through grace of God and personal faith in Jesus Christ

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: 2 Timothy 1:9 gives God's purpose and grace in Christ before time began, not by works. 2 Thessalonians 2:13-14 says God chose believers to be saved and called them through the gospel. Compatibility with human freedom is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is election?
before.answer: Election is God's eternal plan, formed before the world began, to save sinners. Election is consistent with the sovereignty of God and with the freedom of man. Election includes evangelism; God chose to save people through spreading the Gospel. We cannot boast of our salvation. God chose us; we didn't choose Him.
before.right: God's eternal plan, formed before the world began, to save sinners through spreading the Gospel

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: John 6:44 says no one can come to Jesus unless the Father draws him, so coming to Christ is not simply a decision people make on their own. The verse does not explain human sinfulness or the melting of hearts.

before.question: Do people simply make up their minds to become Christians?
before.answer: For a person to come to Christ, God must first work in his or her heart to attract that person to Himself. This is because people are sinful and do not want God to rule their lives. God must first melt their hard hearts.
before.right: God must first work in their hearts to attract them, because people are sinful and unwilling for God's rule

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: John 16:8 says the Spirit convicts the world about sin, righteousness and judgment; Acts 26:18 describes opening eyes to turn from darkness to God and receive forgiveness through faith in Jesus.

before.question: How does the Holy Spirit work in lost people to bring them to Christ?
before.answer: He enables people to understand the truth and makes them appreciate the goodness of Jesus. He "convicts" people of sin and judgment, making them understand its seriousness. He calls people to Jesus as Savior.
before.right: He enables understanding of truth, makes them appreciate Jesus's goodness, convicts of sin and judgment, and calls as Savior

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Paul testifies to repentance to God and faith in the Lord Jesus (Acts 20:21). Acts 16:31 ties faith to salvation, and Isaiah 30:15 ties repentance to being saved. The "two sides of the same coin" image is the author's illustration, not a verse.

before.question: How does God command people to respond in order to be saved?
before.answer: In repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ. Repentance and faith are like two sides of the same coin.
before.right: In repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Acts 3:19 calls sinners to repent and turn back so their sins are wiped away, and Isaiah 55:7 bids the wicked forsake their way and thoughts and return to the LORD. Together they teach turning from sin to God.

before.question: What is repentance?
before.answer: Repentance is a sincere change of mind and of attitude in which the sinner turns to God from sin.
before.right: Repentance is a sincere change of mind and of attitude in which the sinner turns to God from sin

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Saved through faith, not by works (Eph 2:8-9), and "believe in the Lord Jesus" (Acts 16:31) teach trusting Christ alone. The specifics of forgiveness, change, and heaven are not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is saving faith?
before.answer: Faith is trusting Jesus to do things for you that you cannot do for yourself. Faith is trusting Jesus to forgive you, to change your life, and to provide you a home in Heaven. Faith is not just believing with one's mind certain facts about God. Nor is it merely knowing the answers to questions, like those in this booklet. Faith is trusting Christ alone.
before.right: Trusting Jesus to forgive you, change your life, and provide you a home in Heaven

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: 2 Corinthians 5:17 says anyone in Christ is a new creation and the old has passed away. Titus 3:5 speaks of the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit, which together cover the answer.

before.question: What is regeneration?
before.answer: The word "regeneration" means new life. It's another way of saying, "born again." The Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and renews their will, fixing their "want to." This changes the direction of a person's life.
before.right: New life; being born again; the Holy Spirit makes people alive to God and changes their direction

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Deuteronomy 6:4 says "the LORD is One," and Isaiah 44:6 says "there is no God but Me" and "I am the first," which support the claim that there is one God and that he is first.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.doubt: The phrase "best of all beings" appears in none of the shown verses, so that part of the answer goes beyond the text; the oneness of God is what the verses support.

before.question: Who is God?
before.answer: God is the first and best of all beings. There is one and only one living and true God.
before.right: The only living and true God, first and best of all beings

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Believers receive adoption as sons of God through Christ (Gal 4:5; Eph 1:5), receiving the Spirit of sonship and being called God's children (Rom 8:15-16). The special sonship is limited to those who believe.

before.question: What is adoption?
before.answer: When a person becomes a Christian, God makes him or her part of His eternal family. While everyone is God's offspring in the general way of being His creation, only Christians are children of God in this special way.
before.right: When a person becomes a Christian, God makes them part of His eternal family as children of God

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: First Corinthians 6:11 says believers "were sanctified" by the Spirit of God, and Romans 6:22 says those set free to serve God reap fruit that leads to holiness. The indwelling Spirit is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is sanctification?
before.answer: When a person is born again, he or she is set apart from all else for God. Sanctification is the process of growing toward spiritual maturity through the power of the Holy Spirit living within.
before.right: Being set apart for God and growing toward spiritual maturity through the Holy Spirit

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Romans 8:9 says the Spirit of God lives in believers, and 1 Corinthians 12:13 says all believers were baptized into one body in one Spirit. The exact timing "at the very moment" is an inference from these past-tense statements.

before.question: What is the indwelling of the Holy Spirit?
before.answer: At the very moment of salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into the Body of Christ, coming to live inside them from that moment forward.
before.right: At salvation the Holy Spirit baptizes believers into Christ's Body and comes to live inside them

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Shown verses cover assurance (Rom 8:16), leading (Rom 8:14), prayer help (Rom 8:26), character fruit (Gal 5:22-23), witness power (Acts 1:8), gifts (1 Cor 12:7-11), and teaching (John 14:26). Comfort rests on Acts 9:31, not shown.

before.question: What does the Holy Spirit do in the life of believers after they become Christians?
before.answer: The Holy Spirit assures the Christian that he or she is saved. He empowers Christians in developing good character. He helps them to pray and enables them to reach the lost. He gives believers spiritual gifts by which they serve God through His church. He makes them understand the Bible and God's leadership for their lives. The Holy Spirit comforts Christians in sorrow.
before.right: He assures salvation, empowers character development, helps in prayer, gives spiritual gifts, enables witness, opens Scripture, and comforts

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Romans 8:17 and 8:23 speak of the future glorifying and the redemption of our bodies, and 1 John 3:2 says we will be like Jesus and see Him as He is. Freedom from all temptation is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is glorification?
before.answer: Glorification is when God completes salvation. It includes being set totally free from all temptation, being made like Jesus, knowing God perfectly, and receiving a glorified body suited for Heaven. This will be the condition of the saved for all eternity.
before.right: God completing salvation: being freed from temptation, made like Jesus, and receiving a glorified body for eternity

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Jesus says His sheep will never perish and no one can snatch them from His or the Father's hand, and Hebrews says those who hold firmly to the end share in Christ.

before.question: What is the final perseverance of the saints?
before.answer: It means real Christians stick with it. Those who have truly been born again will never become lost again, but shall continue in faith to the end. Believers may stumble into sin for a time, making themselves miserable and grieving the Spirit; yet they shall be kept by the power of God for final salvation. Note: Some refer to this belief as "Once saved, always saved." Unfortunately this term has given some the impression that people can "get saved," live without any sign of God being at work in their lives, and then expect to go to Heaven. The proper term is "perseverance," or "the final perseverance of the saints."
before.right: Real Christians will continue in faith to the end and be kept by God's power for salvation

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Acts 2:41-42 and 1 Corinthians 1:2 show a local gathering of baptized believers, but no shown verse speaks of joining by covenant with Christ and each other or of voluntary membership.

before.question: What is a local New Testament church?
before.answer: A New Testament church is a local congregation of baptized believers, who have voluntarily joined themselves together in covenant with Christ and with each other.
before.right: A local congregation of baptized believers voluntarily joined together in covenant with Christ and each other

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Matthew 28:19-20 gives the mission to make disciples and baptize them. Acts 2:41-47 shows baptism, teaching, breaking of bread, prayer, shared life, praising God, and new converts added. The "colony of heaven" wording is not in these verses.

before.question: What are the purposes of the local church?
before.answer: The church is to glorify God in worship and observe the ordinances of baptism and the Lord's supper. The mission of the church is to spread the gospel of Jesus Christ to the entire world through evangelism and missions. The fellowship of the church is like a "colony of heaven," providing encouragement and accountability to its members.
before.right: To glorify God, observe ordinances, spread the gospel, and provide fellowship and accountability

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Colossians 1:18 supports the Lordship of Christ as Head of the church, but the shown verses do not describe democratic processes. The answer's governance form comes from church teaching.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.doubt: The shown verses describe overseers and shepherds the Holy Spirit appoints (Acts 20:28; 1 Timothy 3) and servant leadership (Mark 10:42-43), not a vote of the members, so "democratic" is not supported by them.

before.question: How is a New Testament church governed?
before.answer: Each congregation operates under the Lordship of Christ through democratic processes. In the decision-making process, this means every member should seek to follow the leading of Jesus Christ as the Head of the church.
before.right: Each congregation operates under Christ's Lordship through democratic processes with Christ as the Head

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: John 4:24 states God is Spirit; Isaiah 6:3 calls Him holy; Psalm 147:5 gives His power and unlimited understanding; Isaiah 40:28 calls Him the everlasting Creator who does not grow weary.

before.question: What is God like?
before.answer: God is Spirit. He is a personal Being, not an impersonal force. God is the Creator, distinct from the creation, existing without needing to be created. He is perfect in holiness and is all-powerful and all-knowing.
before.right: God is Spirit, personal, Creator distinct from creation, perfect, all-powerful and all-knowing

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Philippians 1:1 names overseers and deacons as the church's officers, and 1 Timothy 3:1-13 gives qualifications for both. Ephesians 4:11 names pastors among Christ's gifts. Male-only pastors is drawn from the "husband of one wife" language; women's giftedness is not stated in these passages.

before.question: Who are the Biblical officers of the church?
before.answer: Its scriptural officers are pastors and deacons. Both men and women are gifted for service, but the office of pastor is limited to biblically qualified men.
before.right: Pastors and deacons; pastor office limited to biblically qualified men

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Paul calls the church Christ's body (1 Corinthians 12:27; Colossians 1:24), and Revelation 7:9 shows a multitude from every nation, tribe, people, and tongue. "All ages" is a plain inference, not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is the Church Universal?
before.answer: The New Testament speaks also of the church as the Body of Christ which includes all of the redeemed of all the ages, believers from every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation.
before.right: The Body of Christ including all redeemed of all ages and nations

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Matthew 28:19 commands baptism in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, Romans 6:4 pictures it as burial and rising, and Acts 8:12 ties it to belief; Scripture never calls it the "first ordinance."

before.question: What is the first ordinance of the church?
before.answer: Believer's baptism. Christian baptism is the immersion of a believer beneath water and raising him or her back up -- in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
before.right: Believer's baptism: immersion beneath water in the name of the Trinity

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Acts 2:41 shows those who embraced the message were baptized and then added to the believers that day, so baptism marks entry into the church. The verse does not speak of church membership requirements.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.doubt: The shown verses link baptism with being added to the believers, but nothing shown says baptism is required before observing the Lord's Supper; that part of the answer goes beyond the text.

before.question: Is Baptism required for church membership?
before.answer: Yes. Being a church ordinance, baptism is required to observe the Lord's Supper and before the privileges of church membership.
before.right: Yes. Being a church ordinance, baptism is required to observe the Lord's Supper and before the privileges of church membership

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Galatians 3:2 says the Spirit is received by faith, not works, and 1 Corinthians 12:13 says the Spirit baptizes believers into one body. Water baptism as an outward sign is not stated here.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.doubt: Mark 16:16 and 1 Peter 3:21 link baptism with being saved ("baptism that now saves you"), which sits uneasily with calling baptism only a testimony of prior salvation.

before.question: Is baptism required to become a Christian?
before.answer: Baptism is a testimony that a person has already been saved. It is an outward act representing the inward baptism of the Holy Spirit that really does bring us into the family of God.
before.right: Baptism testifies that a person is already saved; it represents the Spirit's inward baptism bringing us into God's family

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Romans 6:3-5 says those baptized into Christ were baptized into His death, buried with Him, and raised to walk in newness of life, pictured by baptism's death-and-resurrection shape. The "It counts for me" phrasing is the catechism's own gloss.

before.question: What does baptism represent?
before.answer: Baptism pictures what Christ has done for us and in us. It symbolizes Jesus' death and resurrection, testifying, in effect, "It counts for me." It is also a testimony that the believer has died to the old life and has been raised to new life in Christ.
before.right: Jesus' death and resurrection; believer's death to old life and raising to new life in Christ

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Paul tells the church to take bread and cup in remembrance of Jesus, proclaiming His death "until He comes." The verses do not call the act "symbolic" in so many words; that is the catechism's reading of them.

before.question: Baptism is the first of the two ordinances of the church. What is the second?
before.answer: The Lord's Supper. It is a symbolic act in which members of the church eat the bread and drink the cup. They remember the death of Jesus and look forward to His return.
before.right: The Lord's Supper: a symbolic act of eating the bread and drinking the cup, remembering Christ's death

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Matthew 28:1 and Acts 20:7 put the first day of the week at the resurrection and the church's gathering; Revelation 1:10 calls that day the Lord's day, so the answer follows from these verses together.

before.question: What is the Lord's Day?
before.answer: Sunday is the first day of the week and is the Lord's Day -- that is, a day for the Lord. It celebrates the resurrection, since Jesus' resurrection took place on the first day of the week. This day should be respected as a day to spend time with God, in Christian fellowship, and in worship. Since it is a day for the Lord, a Christian should carefully consider the activities the Lord would want him or her to be involved in on this day.
before.right: Sunday, first day celebrating Christ's resurrection; a day for God, fellowship, worship, and pleasing activities

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Psalm 103:19 says God's kingdom rules over all; Luke 17:21 places the kingdom in the midst of people now; Revelation 11:15 says the kingdom has become the Lord's and He will reign forever.

before.question: What is the kingdom of God?
before.answer: In general, God rules over everything in the universe through all of history -- He is the King. The Kingdom means that God rules in a special way in the hearts of His people now. The Kingdom of God will be completed in its fullness when Jesus returns.
before.right: God's rule over all things; God ruling in believers' hearts now; to be completed when Jesus returns

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Acts 1:11 gives Jesus' personal return in the same way He left; Matthew 24:30 adds coming in power and great glory, seen by all; Acts 17:31 gives judgment with justice; 1 Thessalonians 4:16 has the dead in Christ rising.

before.question: How will the world end?
before.answer: According to His promise, Jesus Christ will return personally and visibly to the earth. He will return in glory; everyone will recognize Him and know He is God and in charge. The dead will be raised; and Christ will judge all people in righteousness.
before.right: Jesus will return personally and visibly in glory, raise the dead, and judge all people

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Matthew 28:19 names the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit together, Mark 1:10-11 shows all three distinct at Jesus' baptism, John 1:18 calls the Son God, and 1 Corinthians 8:6 affirms one God.

before.question: What do we mean when we say God is a trinity?
before.answer: God expresses Himself in three Persons-- Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. While each Person of the Trinity has distinct qualities, all three Persons of the Trinity are made of the same stuff. Each Person is fully God, not one-third God. You cannot divide the Trinity; there is only one God.
before.right: Three Persons—Father, Son, Spirit—each fully God, not one-third; there is only one God

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: When the Lord Jesus is revealed, He will inflict vengeance on those who do not know God or obey the gospel. They will suffer eternal destruction, separated from the Lord's presence.

before.question: What will happen to those who don't know Jesus when He returns?
before.answer: The unrighteous will be consigned to Hell, the place of everlasting punishment.
before.right: The unrighteous will be consigned to Hell, the place of everlasting punishment.

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Colossians 3:4 says believers will appear with Christ in glory, and 1 Corinthians 15:43-44 says they are raised in glory and power as spiritual bodies. 2 Timothy 4:8 speaks of the reward, and 1 Thessalonians 4:17 of being always with the Lord.

before.question: What will happen to those who have received Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior at the end of the world?
before.answer: The righteous will appear with Christ in glory, raised in glorified bodies. They will receive their reward and dwell forever in Heaven with the Lord.
before.right: The righteous will have glorified bodies, receive their reward, and dwell forever with the Lord

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Psalm 103:19 says God's throne is in heaven and His kingdom rules over all. Revelation 21:3-4 describes God dwelling with His people, with no more death, mourning, crying, or pain. "Without sin" is not stated outright but follows from this.

before.question: What does the Bible tell us about Heaven?
before.answer: It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering.
before.right: It is the place from which God reigns over the universe. It is a perfect place without sin or suffering

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Matthew 28:19-20 commands going to make disciples of all nations, and 2 Corinthians 5:20 has believers as Christ's ambassadors appealing to others to be reconciled to God. Witness by the example of one's life is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is the responsibility of every Christian?
before.answer: It is the duty of every Christian to seek to win the lost to Christ by telling them about Jesus and by the example of their lives. Every Christian and church should make disciples.
before.right: To win the lost by telling about Jesus and Christian example; every Christian should make disciples

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Jesus commands His followers to make disciples of all nations (Matt 28:19-20), and to be witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth (Acts 1:8). The answer's claims follow from these.

before.question: What is missions?
before.answer: Missions is evangelism that reaches people from another culture or who speak another language. It is not enough to reach people like us in our own community. The Lord Jesus Christ has commanded the preaching of the gospel to all nations.
before.right: Evangelism to people of other cultures and languages; preaching the gospel to all nations

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Paul calls himself a steward of God's mysteries who must be found faithful (1 Cor 4:1-2); Peter says believers are stewards of God's grace in using their gifts (1 Pet 4:10). Ownership of all things is not stated here.

before.question: What is Christian stewardship?
before.answer: Stewardship is managing something that belongs to someone else, using it the way its owner wants it used. Everything we have comes from God and belongs to Him. Christians are stewards of their time, talents, and material possessions. Most importantly, we are stewards of the Gospel.
before.right: Managing God's resources—time, talents, possessions, Gospel—the way God wants

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Second Corinthians 9:7 gives cheerful giving, and 9:6 gives generous giving. First Corinthians 16:2 calls for weekly setting aside of a portion of income, which is regular and grows with income.

before.question: How should the Christian give to the Lord's work?
before.answer: Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give.
before.right: Christians should give to the Lord's work cheerfully, regularly, and generously. The more they make the more they should give

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Genesis 2:24 gives one man and one wife becoming one flesh, Psalm 127:3 calls children a heritage from the LORD, Malachi 2:14 calls the wife a companion "by covenant," and Mark 10:9 says what God joined let no man separate.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.doubt: The opening clause, that the family is "the most important kind of group in human society," is not stated in any of the verses shown, so that part comes from church teaching rather than Scripture.

before.question: What is a family?
before.answer: God created the family as the most important kind of group in human society. Marriage involves one man and one woman, joined by covenant, in a lifetime commitment. Children are a blessing and treasure from the Lord.
before.right: God's creation; one man and one woman in lifetime covenant; children are a blessing

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Ephesians 6:1-4 has children obeying and honoring parents and fathers raising children in the Lord's discipline and instruction; Deuteronomy 6:7 and Titus 2:4-5 add teaching children and training households in love and godliness.

before.question: What is a Christian home supposed to be like?
before.answer: Parents are to be an example to their children of God's good plan for marriage. Parents are to teach their children about God and moral values. They are to lead their children through loving discipline. Children are to honor and obey their parents. They are to learn to make wise choices based on biblical truth.
before.right: Parents exemplify God's plan, teach about God and values, discipline lovingly; children honor parents and learn biblical wisdom

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Acts 16:31 says salvation comes by believing in the Lord Jesus, not by joining a group, and Luke 9:50 says whoever is not against Jesus is for Him. The claim that Baptist teaching comes closest to the Bible is not stated in these verses.

before.question: Are Baptists the only true church?
before.answer: We do not believe Baptists are the only ones going to heaven. One is saved when he or she receives Jesus as Lord and Savior, not by becoming a Baptist. We are Baptists because that set of teachings comes closest to the Bible. Sometimes we cooperate with other Christian denominations on projects of mutual concern.
before.right: No; salvation is through Jesus, not denomination; we cooperate with other Christians on mutual concerns

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Nehemiah 9:6 shows God as Creator and Giver of life, 2 Chronicles 20:6 as ruler over the nations, Colossians 1:14 as the one of whom we have redemption, and Colossians 1:16-17 as Creator who holds all things together.

before.question: How does God relate to the creation?
before.answer: God is the Creator, Redeemer, Preserver, and Ruler of the universe.
before.right: God is the Creator, Redeemer, Preserver, and Ruler of the universe.

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Philippians 4:8 commands believers to think on what is true and excellent, 2 Timothy 4:3 speaks of rejecting sound doctrine, and 1 John 4:1 warns that many false prophets have gone out.
baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.doubt: Titus 2:1 tells Titus to speak what fits sound doctrine rather than to believe only sound doctrine, and no shown verse states "right thinking leads to right living" outright.

before.question: Is what a person believes important?
before.answer: The Bible commands us to think about things that are true and to believe only sound doctrine. Right thinking leads to right living. Christians are warned because there are many false teachers in the world.
before.right: Yes; the Bible commands sound doctrine; right thinking leads to right living

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Luke 1:34-35 gives the Holy Spirit's conception of the virgin's child, John 1:14 says the Word became flesh, Hebrews 1:3 and 1 John 5:20 call Him God's Son and true God; Luke 2:48-49 shows Joseph as father and God as His Father.

before.question: What does the Bible tell us about Jesus?
before.answer: Christ is the eternal Son of God. Joseph took care of Jesus like a dad, but God is His real Father. Conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary, He had a real body and a human spirit. Jesus is fully God and fully human.
before.right: Eternal Son of God, conceived by Holy Spirit, born of Mary, fully God and human

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: Hebrews 4:15 says Jesus was tempted in every way we are yet was without sin. A life free of sin, with no failure in obedience, is what the answer's claim of perfect obedience rests on.

before.question: How good a life did Jesus live?
before.answer: He obeyed all of God's commandments and followed God's will for His life perfectly.
before.right: He obeyed all God's commandments and perfectly followed God's will

baptist-know-the-truth-catechism:know-th.note: 1 Peter 2:24 says Christ "bore our sins in His body on the tree," so His death on the cross bore our sins in our place. The word "substitute" and the explicit mention of forgiveness are drawn from that, not stated.

before.question: Why did Jesus come to earth?
before.answer: To die on the cross as a substitute for our sins. By taking our punishment, He secured the forgiveness of our sins.
before.right: Die on the cross as a substitute for our sins, securing forgiveness

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: Judges 3:9-10 names Othniel son of Kenaz as the deliverer whom the LORD raised up, and says he became Israel's judge. He is the first judge narrated in the book.

before.question: What was the name of the first judge of Israel?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: The passages tell of a blameless man named Job who loses his children and wealth, is struck with boils, and still does not sin against God. The story is in the book of Job.

before.question: Which book of the Bible contains the story of a man who lost his family, health, and wealth but remained faithful to God?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: Herodias's daughter, prompted by her mother, asks for "the head of John the Baptist" on a platter, and Herod has John beheaded in prison. Matthew 14:5 calls him a prophet.

before.question: Who was the prophet who had his head cut off at the request of Herod's stepdaughter?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: Acts 8:27 identifies the man as an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of Candace. Philip explains Isaiah to him in verse 35, and Philip baptizes him in verse 38.

before.question: On the desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza, who heard Philip explain the Scripture from Isaiah and was then baptized by him?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: Matthew 4:18-20 names Simon called Peter as a fisherman who left his nets and followed Jesus. The "closest followers" part is not stated in these verses.

before.question: Which disciple was a fisherman and became one of Jesus' closest followers?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: Matthew 2:11 says the Magi presented gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Silver is not among the gifts named, so it is the one that was not presented.

before.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the gifts the Magi presented to Jesus?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: Genesis 11:9 says the city is called Babel, the place where the LORD confused the language of the whole world. Verse 4 describes the city with a tower reaching to the heavens.

before.question: What was the name of the city where the tower was built to reach heaven?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: 1 Samuel 1:20 says Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son, whom she named Samuel, so Hannah is Samuel's mother.

before.question: Who was the mother of Samuel?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: After Moses died, the LORD spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant, and commanded him to lead the people across the Jordan into the land.

before.question: What was the name of the man who led the Israelites into the Promised Land?

brianchanda-bible-quiz:final-bible-quiz-.note: No shown verse gives the number of books in the Bible. The count of 66 comes from the Protestant canon's division of Scripture into books, not from these passages.

before.question: How many books are in the Bible in total (Protestant canon)?

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: The LORD, the King and Redeemer of Israel, says "I am the first and I am the last, and there is no God but Me," so God is the first and chiefest being.

before.question: Who is the First and Chiefest Being?
before.answer: God is the First and Chiefest Being
before.right: God is the First and Chiefest Being

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Ephesians 1:11 speaks of predestination by the counsel of God's will, who works out everything; Ephesians 3:11 names God's eternal purpose; Ephesians 1:12 gives the aim, the praise of His glory.

before.question: What are the Decrees of God?
before.answer: The Decrees of God are, his Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby, for his own Glory, he has foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.
before.right: God's Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby he foreordained whatsoever comes to pass

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Acts 8:38 has Philip and the eunuch go down into the water and come up out of it, Romans 6:4 speaks of being buried with Christ through baptism, and Matthew 28:19 gives the triune name. Immersion follows from these; the verses do not mention sprinkling.

before.question: How is Baptism rightly administered?
before.answer: Baptism is rightly administered, by Immersion, or dipping the whole Body of the Party in Water, into the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, according to Christ's Institution, and the Practice of the Apostles; and not by the sprinkling or pouring of Water, or dipping some Part of the Body, after the Tradition of Men.
before.right: By immersion or dipping the whole body in water according to Christ's institution.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Those baptized in Acts 2 were added to the believers and devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, and Saul tried to join the disciples. The "particular and orderly church" wording is the catechism's gloss.

before.question: What is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized?
before.answer: It is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized, to give up themselves to some particular and orderly Church of Jesus Christ, that they may walk in all the Commandments and Ordinances of the Lord blameless.
before.right: To give themselves to a particular orderly church and walk in commandments.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Peter calls for repentance and baptism; those who embraced the message were baptized, and then devoted themselves to the breaking of bread. The answer is drawn from these verses by inference.

before.question: Who are the proper Subjects of this Ordinance?
before.answer: They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works.
before.right: They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Scripture requires self-examination before the Supper, recognizing the Lord's body, and faith (2 Cor 13:5). Partaking of Christ is shown in 1 Cor 10:16-17, and putting away old leaven for sincerity and truth in 1 Cor 5:7-8. Eating unworthily brings judgment (1 Cor 11:29).

before.question: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?
before.answer: It is required of them that would worthily partake of the Lord's Supper, that they examine themselves, of their Knowledge to discern the Lord's Body, of their Faith to feed upon him, of their Repentance, Love, and new Obedience; lest coming unworthily, they eat and drink Judgment to themselves.
before.right: Examine themselves for knowledge to discern the Lord's body and faith.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Psalm 62:8 says to pour out your hearts before God; Romans 8:26 names the Spirit's help; 1 John 5:14 names God's will; John 16:23 names Christ's name; Matthew 21:22 names believing; Psalm 32:5 names confession; Philippians 4:6 names thanksgiving.

before.question: What is Prayer?
before.answer: Prayer is an offering up our Desires to God, by the Assistance of the Holy Spirit, for things agreeable to his Will, in the Name of Christ believing, with Confession of our Sins, and thankful Acknowledgment of his Mercies.
before.right: Offering our desires to God by the Spirit for things agreeable to his will.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Jesus says, "this is how you should pray," then gives the prayer himself (Matt 6:9-13), which is the special rule the answer names. The general use of all Scripture is not stated in the shown verses.

before.question: What rule has God given for our direction in prayer?
before.answer: The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in prayer; but the special rule of direction is that prayer which Christ taught his disciples, commonly called the Lord's Prayer.
before.right: The whole Word of God directs us in prayer; especially the Lord's Prayer.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Matt 6:9 gives the preface "Our Father in heaven." Rom 8:15 and Luke 11:13 show God as a Father who gives to His children, Acts 12:5 and 1 Tim 2:1-2 show praying for others.

before.question: What does the Preface of the Lord's Prayer teach us?
before.answer: The Preface of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "Our Father in heaven," teaches us to draw near to God with all holy reverence and confidence, as children to a Father, able and ready to help us; and that we should pray with and for others.
before.right: To approach God with reverence and confidence as children to a Father, and to pray with and for others

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Matthew 6:9 gives the petition "hallowed be Your name." Psalm 67:2-3 asks that God's ways be known and that the peoples praise Him. Ephesians 1:11-12 says God works out everything for the praise of His glory.

before.question: What do we pray for in the first Petition?
before.answer: In the first Petition, which is, "Hallowed be Your name," we pray that God would enable us and others to glorify Him in all that by which He makes Himself known; and that He would dispose all things to His own glory.
before.right: That God would enable us to glorify His name in all by which He makes Himself known and dispose all things to His glory

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Matthew 6:10 gives the petition "Your kingdom come." Revelation 12:10 shows Satan the accuser thrown down, 2 Thessalonians 3:1 the word spreading, and Revelation 22:20 the Lord's coming.

before.question: What do we pray for in the Second Petition?
before.answer: In the second Petition, which is, "Your kingdom come," we pray that Satan's Kingdom may be destroyed, and that the Kingdom of Grace may be advanced, our selves and others brought into it and kept in it, and that the Kingdom of Glory may be hastened.
before.right: That Satan's kingdom be destroyed and the kingdom of grace be advanced.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Matthew 6:10 gives the petition, Psalm 119:36 asks God to turn the heart to his will, and Psalm 103:20-21 describes angels and servants who carry out his word and will.

before.question: What do we pray for in the third Petition?
before.answer: In the third Petition, which is, "Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven," we pray that God by his grace would make us able and willing to know, obey, and submit to his will in all things, as the angels do in heaven.
before.right: That God by his grace makes us willing to know and obey his will.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: David ascribes the kingdom, power and glory to the LORD (1 Chr 29:11); Daniel brings his petitions on God's compassion, not his own merit (Dan 9:18); and "Amen" is the people's response to a prayer (1 Cor 14:16).

before.question: What does the Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer teach?
before.answer: The Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer, "For Yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen," teaches us to take our encouragement in prayer from God only, and in our prayers to praise him, ascribing kingdom, power and glory to him. And in testimony of our desire and assurance to be heard, we say, Amen.
before.right: Teaches us to take encouragement from God alone and to praise him.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Genesis 2:17 gives the command not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, with death as the penalty. Galatians 3:12 says the law's way is doing its commands to live by them, which the answer's "covenant of life upon perfect obedience" summarizes.

before.question: What special Act of Providence did God exercise towards Man in the Estate wherein he was created?
before.answer: When God had created Man, he entered into a Covenant of Life with him, upon Condition of perfect Obedience: forbidding him to eat of the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, upon pain of Death.
before.right: He entered into a Covenant of Life with him, forbidding the Tree of Knowledge on pain of Death

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Hebrews 11:6 says whoever approaches God must believe that He exists, and Psalm 14:1 calls the one who says "There is no God" a fool whose acts are corrupt and vile.

before.question: Ought every One to believe there is a God?
before.answer: Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not.
before.right: Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Through one man's trespass sin and death passed to all, all fell short of God's glory, all were by nature children of wrath, and evil desires from the heart produce actual sins.

before.question: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell?
before.answer: The sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell, consists in the Guilt of Adam's first Sin, the want of Original Righteousness, and the Corruption of his whole Nature, which is commonly called Original Sin; together with all actual Transgressions which proceed from it.
before.right: Guilt of Adam's Sin, want of Original Righteousness, Corruption of Nature, and all actual Transgressions

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Gen 3:8 shows Adam and Eve hiding from God's presence, Gen 3:17 the cursed ground, Eph 2:3 children of wrath, Gal 3:10 under a curse, Rom 6:23 death as wages, Matt 25:46 eternal punishment.

before.question: What is the Misery of that Estate whereinto Man fell?
before.answer: All Mankind by their Fall lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse; and so made liable to all Miseries in this Life, to Death it self, and to the Pains of Hell for ever.
before.right: By their Fall, Mankind lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse, liable to Death and Pains of Hell forever

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Ephesians 1:4-5 says God chose some in Christ before the world's foundation and predestined them according to His will. Galatians 3:22 says the promise comes by faith in Christ to those who believe. The term "covenant of grace" is a later label.

before.question: Did God leave all Mankind to perish in the Estate of Sin and Misery?
before.answer: God, having out of his meer good pleasure, from all Eternity, elected some to Everlasting Life, did enter into a Covenant of Grace, to deliver them out of the Estate of Sin and Misery, and to bring them into an Estate of Salvation by a Redeemer.
before.right: God from all Eternity elected some to Everlasting Life and made a Covenant of Grace to deliver them from Sin and Misery by a Redeemer

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: The Son sent by God was born of a woman and redeems those under the law (Gal 4:4-5). The eternal Word became flesh (John 1:14), is God over all (Rom 9:5), and in Him deity dwells bodily (Col 2:9). He lives forever (Heb 7:24-25).

before.question: Who is the Redeemer of God's Elect?
before.answer: The only Redeemer of God's Elect, is the Lord Jesus Christ; who being the Eternal Son of God, became Man, and so was; and continueth to be God and Man, in two distinct Natures, and one Person for ever.
before.right: The Lord Jesus Christ, the Eternal Son of God who became Man, being God and Man in two distinct Natures and one Person forever

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Acts 3:22 presents Christ as a prophet like Moses, Hebrews 5 and 7 as a priest who suffered and now intercedes forever, and Psalm 2 and Matthew 21 as the installed King.

before.question: What Offices doth Christ execute as our Redeemer?
before.answer: Christ as our Redeemer executeth the Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in his Estate of Humiliation and Exaltation.
before.right: The Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in Humiliation and Exaltation

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Jesus says he has made known to his disciples everything he learned from the Father (John 15:15), and the Spirit of Christ revealed the salvation now preached by the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:11-12).

before.question: How doth Christ execute the Office of a Prophet?
before.answer: Christ executeth the Office of a Prophet, in revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation.
before.right: In revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many (Heb 9:28), makes atonement for the people's sins (Heb 2:17), and always lives to intercede for those who come to God (Heb 7:25).

before.question: How doth Christ execute the Office of a Priest?
before.answer: Christ executeth the Office of a Priest, in his once offering up of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and reconcile us to God, and in making continual Intercession for us.
before.right: In his once offering of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and making continual Intercession

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Psalm 110 has the willing people, the ruler conquering enemies; Isaiah 32:1-2 has the king reigning in righteousness as a shelter; 1 Corinthians 15:25 says He must reign until all enemies are under His feet.

before.question: How doth Christ execute the Office of a King?
before.answer: Christ executeth the Office of a King, in subduing us to himself, in ruling, and defending us, and in restraining and conquering all his and our Enemies.
before.right: In subduing us to himself, ruling and defending us, and conquering all his and our Enemies

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Romans 1:19-20 says what may be known of God is plain to men through His creation, so that they are without excuse. 2 Timothy 3:15 says the Scriptures make one wise for salvation.

before.question: How may we know there is a God?
before.answer: The Light of Nature in Man, and the Works of God plainly declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit only, do it fully and effectually, for the Salvation of Sinners.
before.right: The Light of Nature and God's Works declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit do it fully and effectually for Salvation

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: These verses show Christ laid in a manger, born under the law, humbled to death on a cross, forsaken by God, buried, and held in death's power until God raised Him. Together they teach each part of the answer.

before.question: Wherein did Christ's Humiliation consist?
before.answer: Christ's Humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low Condition; made under the Law, undergoing the Miseries of this Life, the Wrath of God, and the cursed Death of the Cross; in being buried, and continuing under the Power of Death for a time.
before.right: Born in low condition, made under the Law, bearing God's wrath, the cursed death of the Cross, and burial.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: The four parts are each found in these verses: raised on the third day (1 Cor 15:4), taken up into heaven and due to return (Acts 1:11), raised and seated at God's right hand (Eph 1:20), and a appointed day of judgment (Acts 17:31).

before.question: Wherein consisteth Christ's Exaltation?
before.answer: Christ's Exaltation consisteth in his rising again from the Dead on the third Day, in ascending up into Heaven, in sitting at the right Hand of God the Father, and in coming to judg the World at the last Day.
before.right: His rising from the Dead on the third Day, ascending into Heaven, sitting at God's right Hand, and coming to judge the World

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Faith is the gift of God (Eph 2:8), the Spirit strengthens believers so that Christ dwells in their hearts through faith (Eph 3:16-17), and God calls believers into fellowship with His Son (1 Cor 1:9).

before.question: How does the Spirit apply to us the Redemption purchased by Christ?
before.answer: The Spirit applies to us the Redemption purchased by Christ, by working Faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ, in our effectual Calling.
before.right: By working Faith in us and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual Calling

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: The answer's parts are taught across these verses: people are cut to the heart by the gospel (Acts 2:37), eyes are opened from darkness to light (Acts 26:18), God gives a new heart and His Spirit (Ezek 36:26-27), and no one comes unless the Father draws him (John 6:44-45).

before.question: What is effectual Calling?
before.answer: Effectual Calling, is the Work of God's Spirit, whereby, convincing us of our Sin and Misery, enlightening our Minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our Wills, he doth persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ freely offered to us in the Gospel.
before.right: The Spirit's work convincing us of Sin, enlightening us in Christ, renewing our Wills to embrace him

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Romans 3:24 says we are justified freely by God's grace, Romans 4:6-8 describes sins forgiven and not counted, 2 Corinthians 5:21 gives Christ's righteousness to us, and Galatians 2:16 says justification is by faith, not works.

before.question: What is Justification?
before.answer: Justification is an Act of God's free Grace, wherein he pardoneth all our Sins, and accepteth us as Righteous in his sight, only for the Righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by Faith alone.
before.right: God's free Grace pardoning all our sins and accepting us as Righteous through Christ's imputed Righteousness, received by Faith alone.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Ephesians 4:23-24 speaks of being renewed in the mind and putting on the new self created in righteousness and holiness; Romans 6:6 says the old self was crucified so we are no longer slaves to sin.

before.question: What is Sanctification?
before.answer: Sanctification is the Work of God's free Grace, whereby we are renewed in the whole Man after the Image of God, and are enabled more and more to die unto Sin, and live unto Righteousness.
before.right: The Work of God's Grace whereby we are renewed after God's Image, dying to Sin, living unto Righteousness

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Second Timothy 3:16 calls all Scripture God-breathed, and 3:17 says it equips the man of God for every good work. Ephesians 2:20 grounds the church on the apostles and prophets. Together they support the answer.

before.question: What is the Word of God?
before.answer: The Holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are the Word of God, and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience.
before.right: The Holy Scriptures are the Word of God and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Hebrews 12:23 speaks of the spirits of the righteous made perfect, Philippians 1:23 and Luke 23:43 of going to be with Christ, and Isaiah 57:2 and 1 Thessalonians 4:14 of the dead resting as those asleep in Christ.

before.question: What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at their Death?
before.answer: The Souls of Believers are at their Death made perfect in Holiness, and do immediately pass into Glory: And their Bodies being still united to Christ, do rest in their Graves till the Resurrection.
before.right: Their souls are made perfect in Holiness and pass into Glory; their bodies rest in graves till Resurrection

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Believers are raised in glory and power (1 Cor 15:43), Christ confesses them before the Father (Matt 10:32), they hear "Well done" and enter the joy of the Master (Matt 25:23), and they see Him and are always with the Lord (1 John 3:2; 1 Cor 13:12; 1 Thess 4:17).

before.question: What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at the Resurrection?
before.answer: At the Resurrection Believers being raised up in Glory, shall be openly acknowledged, and acquitted in the Day of Judgement, and made perfectly blessed, both in Soul and Body, in the full enjoyment of God, to all Eternity.
before.right: Believers shall be raised in glory, acknowledged, acquitted, and made perfectly blessed in soul and body, enjoying God

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Luke 16:23-24 shows the rich man in torment in Hades, in fire, after death. John 5:28-29 shows the dead in their graves until they come out to the resurrection of judgment.

before.question: But what shall be done to the Wicked at their Death?
before.answer: The Souls of the Wicked shall at their death be cast into the Torments of Hell, and their Bodies lie in their Graves, till the Resurrection and Judgment of the Great Day.
before.right: Their souls are cast into the Torments of Hell, their bodies lie in Graves till Resurrection and Judgment

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: John 5:28-29 says those in their graves will come out to a resurrection of judgment; Matthew 25:41 and 25:46 say the wicked go into eternal fire and eternal punishment with the devil and his angels.

before.question: What shall be done to the Wicked at the Day of Judgment?
before.answer: At the Day of Judgment the Bodies of the Wicked being raised out of their Graves, shall be sentenced together with their Souls, to unspeakable Torments, with the Devil and his Angels for ever.
before.right: Bodies raised and sentenced with their Souls to unspeakable Torments with the Devil and his Angels forever

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:2 is the preface itself: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery," which the answer quotes word for word.

before.question: What is the Preface to the Ten Commandments?
before.answer: The Preface to the Ten Commandments is in these words, "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery."
before.right: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Because the God who called us is holy and we were redeemed with Christ's precious blood, we are to be holy in all we do, keeping God's commands.

before.question: What doth the Preface to the Ten Commandments teach us?
before.answer: The Preface to the Ten Commandments teacheth us, that because God is the LORD, and our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments.
before.right: Because God is the LORD, our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Revelation 1:3 blesses those who read aloud and hear the prophecy, Deuteronomy 17:19 commands reading it all one's days, and Nehemiah 8:8 has the people understand what is read.

before.question: May all Men make use of the Holy Scriptures?
before.answer: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures.
before.right: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Solomon is told to know the God of his father and serve Him; Israel proclaims the LORD as their God; Jesus says worship the Lord your God and serve Him only; Psalm 29 calls for ascribing glory and worship to Him.

before.question: What is required in the first Commandment?
before.answer: The first Commandment requireth us, to know and acknowledge God to be the only true God, and our God; and to worship and glorify him accordingly.
before.right: To know and acknowledge God as the only true God, and to worship and glorify him

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:3 forbids having other gods before the LORD, and Romans 1:21 condemns those who did not glorify God as God. Together they teach the answer's forbidden denial, neglect, and misdirected worship.

before.question: What is forbidden in the first Commandment?
before.answer: The first commandment forbids denying, or not worshipping and glorifying, the true God as God and our God, and giving to any other the worship and glory that are due to him alone.
before.right: Forbids denying or not worshipping the true God, and giving his worship and glory to another.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: God sees the idolatry Israel's elders commit in secret, though they say "The LORD does not see us," and He answers with wrath, refusing pity or to listen. The answer follows from these verses.

before.question: What are we specially taught by these words "before me" in the first Commandment?
before.answer: These words "before me" in the first Commandment, teach us, that God who seeth all things, taketh notice of, and is much displeased with the Sin of having any other God.
before.right: That God sees all things and is displeased with having any other god.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:4-6 states the second commandment word for word: no idol in the form of anything in heaven, earth, or waters, and no bowing down or worshiping them, because the LORD is a jealous God.

before.question: Which is the second Commandment?
before.answer: The second Commandment is, "You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath. You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me, but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments."
before.right: You shall not make an idol for yourself, nor bow down to it or worship it.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Acts 2:42 shows believers devoted to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer, and Deut 4:2 forbids adding to or subtracting from God's commands, so the answer is taught from these verses.

before.question: What is required in the second Commandment?
before.answer: The second Commandment requireth, the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances, as God hath appointed in his Word.
before.right: The receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances as God appointed

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Deuteronomy 4:15-16 forbids making any form or shape as an idol, and 12:32 forbids adding to or subtracting from what God commands, so worship by images or other unappointed ways is forbidden.

before.question: What is forbidden in the second Commandment?
before.answer: The second Commandment forbiddeth the worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word.
before.right: The worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Psalm 95:3 calls the LORD a great King above all gods (sovereignty); Psalm 95:6-7 says he is our Maker and our God (propriety); Exodus 20:5 says he is a jealous God (zeal).

before.question: What are the Reasons annexed to the second Commandment?
before.answer: The Reasons annexed to the second Commandment are, God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he has to his own Worship.
before.right: God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he has to his own Worship

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: The verses teach honoring God's name, works, and ways, so reverent use of God's names, attributes, works, word, and ordinances follows from them; Malachi 1:11 ties worship in His name to His name's greatness.

before.question: What is required in the third Commandment?
before.answer: The third Commandment requireth, the Holy and Reverent Use of God's Names, Titles, Attributes, Ordinances, Word, and Works.
before.right: Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, word, and works.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Paul calls Timothy to hold the pattern of sound teaching, which is what to believe, and says Scripture gives instruction and training in righteousness, which is what God requires of us.

before.question: What things are chiefly contained in the Holy Scriptures?
before.answer: The Holy Scriptures chiefly contain, what Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man.
before.right: What Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: God's Sabbaths are given as a sign so that Israel may know He is the LORD, and Israel profaned them; Malachi 1:12 condemns profaning the LORD's table. Together these teach that profaning what makes God known is forbidden.

before.question: What is forbidden in the third Commandment?
before.answer: The third Commandment forbiddeth all profaning and abusing of any thing, whereby God makes himself known.
before.right: Forbiddeth the profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:7 says the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain, which is the reason the answer gives for the third commandment. Deuteronomy 5:11 says the same.

before.question: What is the Reason annexed to the third Commandment?
before.answer: The Reason annexed to the third Commandment, is, that however the breakers of this Commandment may escape Punishment from Men, yet the Lord our God will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment.
before.right: Breakers may escape Men's Punishment, but the Lord will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:8-11 gives the fourth commandment itself, beginning "Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy," and the answer quotes that text.

before.question: Which is the fourth Commandment?
before.answer: The fourth Commandment is, "Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work—neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates. For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy."
before.right: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy; six days you shall labor, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:10 names the seventh day as the Sabbath. Acts 20:7 and Revelation 1:10 show the church gathering on the first day, which John calls the Lord's day, supporting the first-day answer by inference.

before.question: Which Day of the Seven has God appointed to be the Weekly Sabbath?
before.answer: Before the Resurrection of Christ, God appointed the seventh day of the week to be the weekly Sabbath, and the first day of the week ever since, to continue to the end of the world, which is the Christian Sabbath.
before.right: Before Christ's Resurrection, the seventh day; since then, the first day of the week.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:8,10 gives holy rest with no work; Isaiah 58:13 forbids seeking one's own pleasure and calls for honoring the day; Matthew 12:12 allows doing good. Worship all day is not stated here.

before.question: How is the Sabbath to be sanctified?
before.answer: The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy Resting all that Day, even from such worldly Employments and Recreations as are lawful on other Days; and spending the whole Time in the Public and Private Exercises of God's Worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the Works of Necessity and Mercy.
before.right: By holy Resting from worldly Employments, spending the Time in God's Worship, except Works of Necessity and Mercy

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Isaiah 58:13 forbids seeking one's own pleasure or speaking idle words on the holy day. Amos 8:5 condemns worldly business on the Sabbath. Ezekiel 22:26 and Malachi 1:13 condemn disregarding the Sabbath and careless performance of worship.

before.question: What is forbidden in the fourth Commandment?
before.answer: The fourth Commandment forbiddeth the Omission or careless Performance of the Duties required, and the profaning the Day by Idleness, or doing that which is in it self sinful; or by unnecessary Thoughts, Words, or Works about worldly Employments or Recreations.
before.right: Forbiddeth omission or careless performance of duties, and profaning the day by idleness.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:9-11 gives the reasons: six days for labor, the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD, God rested after creating in six days, and He blessed and sanctified the Sabbath day.

before.question: What are the Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment?
before.answer: The Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment, are God's allowing us six Days of the Week for our own lawful Employments, his challenging a special Propriety in a Seventh, his own Example, and his blessing the Sabbath Day.
before.right: God's allowing six days for lawful employments, claiming the seventh, his example, and blessing.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:12 states the command outright: "Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you."

before.question: Which is the fifth Commandment?
before.answer: The fifth Commandment is, "Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you."
before.right: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Romans 12:10 calls for honoring one another, 1 Peter 2:17 for treating everyone with high regard and honoring the king, and Ephesians 5:21 for mutual submission, covering equals, superiors and inferiors.

before.question: What is required in the fifth Commandment?
before.answer: The fifth Commandment requireth the preserving the Honour, and performing the Duties belonging to every one in their several Places and Relations, as Superiours, Inferiors, or Equals.
before.right: Requireth preserving honour and performing duties in their several places and relations.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Matthew 15:4-6 condemns leaving parents unhonored, Ezekiel 34:2-4 condemns shepherds neglecting their flock, and Romans 13:7 says to give honor to whom honor is due. Together they teach the answer's general principle.

before.question: What is forbidden in the fifth Commandment?
before.answer: The fifth Commandment forbiddeth the neglecting of, or doing any thing against the Honor and Duty which belongeth to every one in their several Places and Relations.
before.right: Forbiddeth neglecting or doing anything against honour and duty in places and relations.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Ephesians 6:2-3 calls the command "the first commandment with a promise" and gives the promise that it may go well with you and that you may have a long life on the earth. The parenthetical qualifier about God's glory is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is the Reason annexed to the fifth Commandment?
before.answer: The reason annexed to the fifth Commandment, is a Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it shall serve for God's Glory, and their own Good) to all such as keep this Commandment.
before.right: A Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it serves God's Glory) to all who keep it

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:13 gives the text, "You shall not murder," which is the sixth item in the Ten Commandments list in Exodus 20 when counted in order.

before.question: What is the sixth Commandment?
before.answer: The sixth Commandment is, "You shall not murder."
before.right: The sixth Commandment is, "You shall not murder."

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Ephesians 5:29 says no one hates his own body but nourishes and cherishes it, which supports preserving one's own life. In 1 Kings 18:4 Obadiah hides and feeds the prophets, preserving others' lives.

before.question: What is required in the sixth Commandment?
before.answer: The sixth Commandment requires all lawful endeavors to preserve our own life, and the life of others.
before.right: All lawful endeavors to preserve our own life, and the life of others

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Gen 9:6 forbids shedding a man's blood, Acts 16:28 forbids harming oneself, and Lev 19:16 forbids endangering a neighbor's life, which together teach the answer's forbidden taking of life, one's own or a neighbor's.

before.question: What is forbidden in the sixth Commandment?
before.answer: The sixth Commandment absolutely forbiddeth the taking away of our own Life; or the Life of our Neighbor unjustly, or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.
before.right: Absolutely forbiddeth taking away our own life or our neighbor's life unjustly.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Scripture teaches chastity in each part: 1 Corinthians 7:2 guards purity in marriage, 1 Peter 3:2 pure behavior, Ephesians 5:4 forbids impure speech, and Matthew 5:28 forbids lust in the heart.

before.question: What is required in the seventh Commandment?
before.answer: The seventh Commandment requireth the preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity, in heart, speech, and behavior.
before.right: Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart, speech, and behavior.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Matthew 5:28 forbids lust in the heart (thoughts), and Ephesians 5:3-4 forbids sexual immorality and impurity in action and obscenity and crude joking in speech, so the answer follows from these verses.

before.question: What is forbidden in the seventh Commandment?
before.answer: The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.
before.right: The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Scripture commands providing for one's own household (1 Tim 5:8), returning a enemy's stray ox to him (Exod 23:4), and helping a destitute countryman so he can live (Lev 25:35). Together these teach the answer's care for our own and others' estate.

before.question: What is required in the eighth Commandment?
before.answer: The eighth Commandment requireth the lawful procuring, and furthering the Wealth and outward Estate of our selves, and others.
before.right: Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of ourselves and others.

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Leviticus 19:13 forbids defrauding or robbing a neighbor, and Ephesians 4:28 forbids stealing. Proverbs 23:21 warns that gluttony and drowsiness bring poverty, covering hindrance of one's own wealth.

before.question: What is forbidden in the eighth Commandment?
before.answer: The eighth Commandment forbiddeth whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate.
before.right: Whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Exodus 20:16 gives the wording "You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor." Counting the ten commandments in Exodus 20 in order, it falls ninth, before the command not to covet.

before.question: Which is the ninth Commandment?
before.answer: The ninth Commandment is, "You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor."
before.right: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:1695_bap.note: Zechariah 8:16 commands speaking truth to one another and true judgments; Proverbs 14:5 and 3 John 1:12 show the honest witness and a good testimony, covering truthful witness and a good name.

before.question: What is required in the ninth Commandment?
