before.answer: The moral law is of use to all men, to inform them of the holy nature and will of God, and of their duty, binding them to walk accordingly; to convince them of their disability to keep it, and of the sinful pollution of their nature, hearts, and lives; to humble them in the sense of their sin and misery, and thereby help them to a clearer sight of the need they have of Christ, and of the perfection of his obedience.
before.right: Informs of God's will and duty, convinces of sin and inability, humbles us, and shows our need of Christ

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.note: The law leads people to Christ (Gal 3:24), its accusing conscience (Rom 2:15), leaves men without excuse (Rom 1:20), and those who rely on works lie under its curse (Gal 3:10).

before.question: What particular use is there of the moral law to unregenerate men?
before.answer: The moral law is of use to unregenerate men, to awaken their consciences to flee from wrath to come, and to drive them to Christ; or, upon their continuance in the estate and way of sin, to leave them inexcusable, and under the curse thereof.
before.right: Awakens consciences to flee wrath and drive to Christ; or if sin continues, leaves inexcusable and under curse

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.note: Believers are not under the law but under grace (Rom 6:14); Christ bore the law's curse for them (Gal 3:13) and fulfilled its righteous standard in them (Rom 8:3-4), calling them to zeal for good works (Titus 2:14).

before.question: What special use is there of the moral law to the regenerate?
before.answer: Although they that are regenerate, and believe in Christ, be delivered from the moral law as a covenant of works, so as thereby they are neither justified nor condemned; yet, besides the general uses thereof common to them with all men, it is of special use, to show them how much they are bound to Christ for his fulfilling it, and enduring the curse thereof in their stead, and for their good; and thereby to provoke them to more thankfulness, and to express the same in their greater care to conform themselves thereunto as the rule of their obedience.
before.right: Regenerate delivered from law as covenant; law shows how bound to Christ for fulfilling it and enduring curse, provoking thankfulness

creeds-json-reformed-catechisms:westmins.note: The rules are drawn from the shown passages: the law is perfect (Ps 19:7; Jas 2:10), spiritual (Rom 7:14), reaches inward thoughts (Matt 5:21-28), covers related sins (Col 3:5), and calls us to help others (Lev 19:17; Eph 4:28; Gen 18:19).

before.question: What rules are to be observed for the right understanding of the ten commandments?
before.answer: For the right understanding of the ten commandments, these rules are to be observed: 1. That the law is perfect, and bindeth everyone to full conformity in the whole man unto the righteousness thereof, and unto entire obedience forever; so as to require the utmost perfection of every duty, and to forbid the least degree of every sin. 2. That it is spiritual, and so reaches the understanding, will, affections, and all other powers of the soul; as well as words, works, and gestures. 3. That one and the same thing, in divers respects, is required or forbidden in several commandments. 4. That as, where a duty is commanded, the contrary sin is forbidden; and, where a sin is forbidden, the contrary duty is commanded: so, where a promise is annexed, the contrary threatening is included; and, where a threatening is annexed, the contrary promise is included. 5. That what God forbids, is at no time to be done; What he commands, is always our duty; and yet every particular duty is not to be done at all times. 6. That under one sin or duty, all of the same kind are forbidden or commanded; together with all the causes, means, occasions, and appearances thereof, and provocations thereunto. 7. That what is forbidden or commanded to ourselves, we are bound, according to our places, to endeavor that it may be avoided or performed by others, according to the duty of their places. 8. That in what is commanded to others, we are bound, according to our places and callings, to be helpful to them; and to take heed of partaking with others in: What is forbidden them.
before.right: The law is perfect binding to complete conformity, spiritual reaching all powers, with duties commanded and sins forbidden in commandments

before.question: What did the people of the island think when they saw no harm come to Paul?
before.answer: They thought that he was a god
before.right: They thought that he was a god

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 28:7 says Publius, the chief official of the island, welcomed Paul and his companions and entertained them hospitably for three days.

before.question: Who treated Paul and his friends kindly on Malta?
before.answer: Publius, the chief official of the island
before.right: Publius, the chief official of the island

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 28:8 says the father of Publius lay sick with fever and dysentery, and Paul prayed, laid hands on him, and healed him. The answer matches.

before.question: What did Paul do for the ruler Publius?
before.answer: He made his sick father well
before.right: He made his sick father well

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul's party sailed from Malta in an Alexandrian ship, stopped at Syracuse, Rhegium and Puteoli, and came to Rome. Rome lies in Italy, so the answer follows, though Italy is not named in these verses.

before.question: To what land did they sail from the island of Malta?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 28:14 says that after staying a week with brothers at Puteoli, "And so we came to Rome," so the journey ends at Rome. Acts 28:16 confirms it: "When we arrived in Rome."

before.question: At what great city did Paul's long journey end?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 28:16 places Paul in Rome under a soldier's guard, and Acts 28:30 says he stayed there two full years in his own rented house. The answer "two years" follows from these verses.

before.question: How long was Paul a prisoner at Rome?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 28:30-31 says that while living in his rented house for two years, Paul boldly proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ. That is the gospel, though the word itself is not used.

before.question: What did Paul do during his two years in Rome, living in his own rented house?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul writes, "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith," as he faces his departure (2 Tim 4:6-7).

before.question: What did Paul write near the end of his life?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 2:15 says that after Pharaoh sought to kill Moses, Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, which answers the question.

before.question: To what land did Moses go after he grew up?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: At Pentecost, Peter stands up with the Eleven and addresses the crowd as their spokesman, showing him taking the lead in the early church. Scripture does not use the word "leader."

before.question: Who was the leader of the church in its early days?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 13:1 places Barnabas and Saul in the church at Antioch, and Acts 13:3 says that after fasting and prayer its members laid hands on them and sent them off.

before.question: According to Acts 13:1-3, which church sent off Barnabas and Saul on their missionary journey?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Genesis 3:23-24 says the LORD God banished the man from the Garden of Eden and drove him out, which answers the question.

before.question: What became of them when they did not obey God's word?
before.answer: They were driven out of the garden
before.right: They were driven out of the garden

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 7:29 says Moses fled to Midian and lived there as a foreigner. Acts 7:30 says forty years later the angel appeared to him at the burning bush, so the stay lasted forty years.

before.question: How long was Moses in the land of Midian?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: While the church at Antioch was worshiping and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to set apart Barnabas and Saul; Acts 13:4 says they were sent forth by the Holy Spirit.

before.question: Who were the two missionaries sent out from the church at Antioch?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 21:33 records the commander arresting Paul and ordering him bound with two chains, and Acts 21:31 places the scene in Jerusalem, where the city is in turmoil and Paul is seized at the temple.

before.question: Where was Paul arrested by the Roman commander and bound with two chains?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 3:1 says Moses was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Jethro when he came to Horeb, the mountain of God, where the angel appeared in the bush.

before.question: When the angel of the LORD appeared to Moses in the burning bush, what was Moses' work?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 3:1 says Moses came to Horeb, the mountain of God, where he saw the bush ablaze but not consumed, a marvelous sight. The "also called Mount Sinai" part is not stated in these verses.

before.question: On what mountain did Moses see a wonderful sight?
before.answer: On Mount Horeb, called also Mount Sinai
before.right: On Mount Horeb, called also Mount Sinai

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 3:4 says the LORD saw Moses coming and God called out to him from within the bush. The verses name the speaker as the LORD and God, though "of Israel" is not in the text.

before.question: What spoke to Moses from the burning bush?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: At the bush God says, "I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt," which matches the printed answer.

before.question: At the burning bush, what did God tell Moses to do?
before.answer: To bring his people out of Egypt
before.right: To bring his people out of Egypt

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, says he will not let Israel go, so Exodus 5:2 names him as the one refusing Israel's release.

before.question: Who would not allow the Israelites to go out of Egypt?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The LORD sends a series of plagues on Egypt, such as frogs (8:2) and swarms of flies that ruin the land (8:24), while Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go. The answer "many plagues" follows from the sequence.

before.question: What came upon Pharaoh and the Egyptians until they were willing to let the Israelites go?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Timothy 2:4 says God "wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth," which matches the printed answer almost word for word.

before.question: What is God's will concerning man?
before.answer: God wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
before.right: God wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus names as the first and greatest command loving God with all the heart, soul, and mind, so the Law reaches inward devotion, not just outward conduct.

before.question: Does God's Law demand outward observance only?
before.answer: No; it demands the whole man, and the willing obedience of heart and mind
before.right: No; it demands the whole man, and the willing obedience of heart and mind

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 104 shows all creatures depending on God for food, breath, and life, and Matthew 6:26 shows the heavenly Father feeding the birds, which together teach the answer.

before.question: How does God preserve all things?
before.answer: He lets all things continue as long as He thinks well, and He cares like a father for all His creatures
before.right: He lets all things continue as long as He thinks well, and cares like a father for all creatures

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Timothy 4:10 calls God the Savior of everyone and especially of those who believe, which matches the answer. Matthew 6:26 adds that people are far more valuable to the Father than birds.

before.question: For whom does God care most?
before.answer: For man; and especially for His believing children
before.right: For man; and especially for His believing children

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 8:28 says God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, and Genesis 50:20 shows God turning evil intended by men to good. The verses do not spell out that God permits sin or limits it.

before.question: How does God govern men with regard to their sins?
before.answer: He suffers them to sin, sets limits to their sinning, and so guides the result that everything will be for their good who love Him
before.right: He allows sin, limits sinning, and guides results for the good of those who love Him

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 11:33 says God's judgments are unsearchable and His ways untraceable, so we do not always understand them. Hosea 14:9 says the LORD's ways are right. "Kindest and best" is drawn from these, not stated outright.

before.question: Do we always understand the ways of God's providence?
before.answer: No; His ways are often hidden from our eyes; but even then they are the kindest and best
before.right: No; His ways are often hidden from our eyes; but even then they are the kindest and best

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 121:7 says the LORD will guard you from all evil and preserve your soul, which matches the answer that God keeps and protects the believer from all evil.

before.question: In whose care may you therefore safely leave yourself?
before.answer: In God's care, who protects me from all danger, and keeps me from all evil
before.right: In God's care, who protects me from all danger, and keeps me from all evil

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: God gave His own Son for us and will freely give us all things (Romans 8:32), and He shows mercy to all (Romans 11:32), so His gifts rest on mercy rather than on our desert.

before.question: Have you deserved all this?
before.answer: Not in the least; He does all this, not because I have deserved it, but because He is a loving and merciful Father
before.right: Not in the least; He does this because He is a loving and merciful Father, not by desert

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 116:12-13 asks how to repay the LORD's goodness and answers with grateful worship. Luke 17:10 calls faithful service our duty. Together they teach the answer, though "all the days of my life" is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What do you owe God for all his goodness?
before.answer: It is my duty to serve Him thankfully and obediently all the days of my life
before.right: It is my duty to serve Him thankfully and obediently all the days of my life

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses name angels as heavenly servants of God (Psalm 103:20, Hebrews 1:14), but none ranks holy angels as the most excellent heavenly creatures; that ranking comes from catechism teaching.

before.question: Which are the most excellent of the heavenly creatures?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 103:20-21 has the angels blessing the LORD and doing His word and will, which is praise and service. Hebrews 1:14 calls them ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.

before.question: What is the work of the holy angels?
before.answer: They praise God, and serve Him, especially by ministering to His children
before.right: They praise God, and serve Him, especially by ministering to His children

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: God did not spare the angels who sinned; they are kept in chains of darkness for judgment, and the eternal fire is prepared for the devil and his angels. Conceit brought the devil's condemnation (1 Tim 3:6). "King" is implied, not stated.

before.question: Are there not also evil angels?
before.answer: Yes; there are evil angels who have fallen away from God through pride and disobedience, and are forever excluded from fellowship with Him. The devil is their king
before.right: Yes; evil angels fell through pride and disobedience, forever excluded from God. The devil is their king

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 3:20 and Galatians 2:16 say no one is justified by works of the law, and Isaiah 64:6 says even our righteous acts are like filthy rags. The "since the fall" framing is not stated, but the shown verses support the answer.

before.question: Can we be saved through the Law?
before.answer: No; since the fall in sin no man can perfectly keep the Law
before.right: No; since the fall in sin no man can perfectly keep the Law

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: God makes man in His own image to rule over the fish, birds, livestock and every creature on the earth, and blesses him with that rule. The verses teach man's rank above the other creatures, though they do not use the word "most excellent."

before.question: Which is the most excellent of the earthly creatures?
before.answer: Man, to whom God gave power to rule over the earth
before.right: Man, to whom God gave power to rule over the earth

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: God made man in His own image and likeness (Gen 1:26-27), and God saw all He had made as very good (Gen 1:31). Sinlessness is implied because the sin entered only later, at the fall.

before.question: What was the character of man as he was made by God?
before.answer: Adam and Eve were innocent, without sin, and like God
before.right: Adam and Eve were innocent, without sin, and like God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 4:24 says the new self is created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness, and Colossians 3:10 speaks of renewal in knowledge in the image of the Creator. Wisdom, peace and joy are traditional additions.

before.question: In what did the image of God in man consist?
before.answer: In true wisdom, righteousness and holiness, peace and joy
before.right: In true wisdom, righteousness and holiness, peace and joy

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Adam is placed in Eden, with the tree of life, free to eat from the garden, and Genesis 3:22 implies he could have lived forever by eating from that tree. Health and freedom from care are inferred, not stated.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The verses show Paradise, free eating, and access to the tree of life, but they do not say "perfect health" or link these benefits to the image of God itself.

before.question: What benefit did the human body have from the image of God?
before.answer: Perfect health, immortality, and a life free from care in Paradise
before.right: Perfect health, immortality, and a life free from care in Paradise

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The serpent denies God's word ("You will not surely die"), the woman wants to be like God and gain wisdom, and she eats what was forbidden. Doubt, self-seeking, and disobedience all appear.

before.question: In what did the sin of Adam and Eve consist?
before.answer: It consisted especially in the unbelief of their hearts and in their selfishness and disobedience
before.right: It consisted especially in the unbelief of their hearts and in their selfishness and disobedience

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Eve says the serpent deceived her, and Revelation identifies that ancient serpent as the devil, the deceiver of the whole world. Their consent to eat (Gen 3:6) supports the "permitted" wording.

before.question: Who led them astray?
before.answer: They permitted the devil to lead them astray
before.right: They permitted the devil to lead them astray

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 4:18 says those walking in sinful ways are "darkened in their understanding," with ignorance rooted in the hardness of their hearts, which matches the answer.

before.question: How has sin injured the human soul?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 6:13 warns against presenting the body's parts to sin as instruments of wickedness, Psalm 38:3 links bodily sickness to God's anger over sin, and James 1:15 says sin gives birth to death.

before.question: How has sin injured the human body?
before.answer: Sin has made the body a tool of every evil passion, and has brought upon it disease, distress, countless pains, and finally death
before.right: Made body tool of evil passion, brought disease, distress, pain, death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 3:16 says God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, so that whoever believes shall not perish but have eternal life. This answers that God does not leave people to perish.

before.question: Will God, then, leave all men to perish?
before.answer: No; God has in love sent His Son Jesus Christ to save man
before.right: No; God has in love sent His Son Jesus Christ to save man

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 3:20 says the law brings awareness of sin, showing our sins; Romans 4:15 says the law brings wrath, the wrath that falls on sin.

before.question: Of what benefit, then, is the Law?
before.answer: It points out to us our sins and the wrath of God toward sin
before.right: It points out to us our sins and the wrath of God toward sin

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Genesis 3:15 is God's first promise of a deliverer, the seed of the woman who will crush the serpent's head. It is spoken right after the fall in 3:6, in the curse on the serpent.

before.question: When was this Savior first promised to the world?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Galatians 4:4 says that when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, so the answer's wording comes directly from the verse. The phrase "appointed and prepared by God Himself" follows from God doing the sending.

before.question: When was Christ sent to the world?
before.answer: When the time had fully come; that is, the time appointed and prepared by God Himself
before.right: When the time had fully come, the time appointed and prepared by God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 1:1 shows the Word is God, and John 1:14 says the Word became flesh. Luke 1:31 has Mary bearing a son, and Luke 1:35 calls the child the Son of God.

before.question: Who is Jesus Christ?
before.answer: The Son of God and the Son of Mary, true God and true man
before.right: The Son of God and the Son of Mary, true God and true man

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 1:1-2 says the Word was God and was with God in the beginning; John 1:14 calls Him the one and only Son from the Father. The answer's "begotten... from eternity" is drawn from these verses, though "begotten" is the church's wording, not the BSB's.

before.question: How does Christ have divine nature?
before.answer: He is begotten of the Father from eternity
before.right: He is begotten of the Father from eternity

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 1:18 calls Jesus "the one and only Son, who is Himself God," and John 10:30 says, "I and the Father are one," which together answer the question.

before.question: What does the Bible say about Christ being true God?
before.answer: The Bible calls Him the one and only Son of God, and one with the Father
before.right: The Bible calls Him the one and only Son of God, and one with the Father

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 1:14 states that the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, which is the printed answer quoted directly; the Word who is God (John 1:1) took on human flesh.

before.question: What does the Bible say about Christ being both God and man?
before.answer: It says, The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us
before.right: It says, The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Hebrews 2:14 says He shared our flesh and blood so that by His death He might destroy the devil. Hebrews 2:17 says He had to be made like His brothers to make atonement for the people's sins. Together they teach that His becoming man was for His suffering and death for us.

before.question: Why must the Son of God become true man?
before.answer: In order that He might suffer and die for us
before.right: In order that He might suffer and die for us

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Christ entered the Most Holy Place by His own blood, securing eternal redemption, and offered Himself through the eternal Spirit, so His blood has lasting power to cleanse.

before.question: Why must our Savior be true God?
before.answer: In order that His death and His blood might have everlasting power to atone for sin
before.right: In order that His death and His blood might have everlasting power to atone for sin

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The angel says the Holy Spirit will come upon Mary and the Holy One to be born will be called the Son of God. Sinlessness is inferred from the Spirit's conception and the title "Holy One," not stated outright.

before.question: Is Jesus conceived and born with sin?
before.answer: No; He is conceived by the Holy Spirit and therefore without sin
before.right: No; He is conceived by the Holy Spirit and therefore without sin

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus names love to the Lord God and love to one's neighbor as the first and second commandments, and says all the Law and the Prophets hang on these two.

before.question: What is the substance of the law?
before.answer: Love to God and to our neighbor
before.right: Love to God and to our neighbor

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 4:25 gives "Messiah" with the note "(called Christ)," so Christ is the same name as Messiah. The meaning "Anointed" is a language point not stated in the verses shown.

before.question: What does the name Christ signify?
before.answer: The same as Messiah; that is, the Anointed or the Consecrated
before.right: The same as Messiah; that is, the Anointed or the Consecrated

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 10:38 says God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, which is the answer almost word for word.

before.question: How was Jesus anointed?
before.answer: He was anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power
before.right: He was anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 4:18 shows Christ anointed to preach (prophet), Hebrews 1:9 anointed with a throne and scepter (king), and Hebrews 5:10 designates Him high priest. The three offices are drawn from these together.

before.question: For what offices was Jesus anointed and consecrated?
before.answer: The offices of High Priest, Prophet, and King
before.right: The offices of High Priest, Prophet, and King

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 11:26 states that the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch. The gloss "the anointed" is not in the verse; it comes from the Greek word Christos.

before.question: How are the believers named after Christ?
before.answer: They are called Christians; meaning, "the anointed"
before.right: They are called Christians; meaning, "the anointed"

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Peter says we were redeemed with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish; Paul says He was born under the law to redeem those under it; Romans 5:19 credits the obedience of the one man.

before.question: With what means has Christ redeemed us?
before.answer: He has paid for our sins with His holy and precious blood and His innocent death, and He has fulfilled the law in our stead with His holy life and His perfect obedience
before.right: Paid for sins with His precious blood and innocent death; fulfilled law through obedience

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 31:5 says "You have redeemed me," and 1 Timothy 1:15 says Christ came to save sinners, with Paul as the worst. Romans 8:1 speaks of no condemnation for those in Christ.

before.question: Whom has Christ redeemed?
before.answer: He has redeemed me, a lost and condemned sinner
before.right: He has redeemed me, a lost and condemned sinner

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus names loving the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind as the first and greatest commandment, which the catechism takes as the substance of the first table of the Law.

before.question: What is the substance of the first table?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Timothy 2:6 says Christ "gave Himself as a ransom for all," which is the answer's wording, so the answer comes directly from this verse.

before.question: Has not Christ redeemed all mankind?
before.answer: Yes, He has; He gave Himself as a ransom for all
before.right: Yes, He has; He gave Himself as a ransom for all

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Titus 2:14 says Christ redeemed us to purify a people for His own possession, zealous for good deeds; Colossians 1:13 places us in the kingdom of His beloved Son. The "righteousness, innocence, and happiness" wording is only loosely drawn from these.

before.question: For what purpose has Christ redeemed you?
before.answer: He has redeemed me in order that I might be His own, live with Him in His kingdom, and serve Him in righteousness, innocence, and happiness
before.right: Redeemed me to be His own, live in His kingdom, and serve in righteousness

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses describe Christ's humbling, suffering, crucifixion, death, and burial (Phil 2:8, Matt 20:19, Rom 6:4), but none numbers them as five steps. The count is a later Lutheran teaching.

before.question: How many steps do you notice in the humiliation of Christ?
before.answer: Five: the birth in poverty; the suffering; the crucifixion; the death; the burial
before.right: Five: the birth in poverty; the suffering; the crucifixion; the death; the burial

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The verses place the sorrow of Gethsemane, Jesus being handed over to sinners, binding, flogging, the crown of thorns, and crucifixion in the night and on Good Friday, though none says these were the greatest suffering.

before.question: When was the suffering of Christ greatest?
before.answer: In the night before His death, and on Good Friday, when He was delivered into the hands of His enemies, and was bound, beaten, scourged, crowned with thorns, and finally nailed to the cross
before.right: Night before death and Good Friday, when He was bound, beaten, scourged, crowned, crucified

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 26:38 says Christ's soul was consumed with sorrow to the point of death, and Isaiah 53:11 speaks of the anguish of His soul as He bears their iniquities. His suffering went beyond the body.

before.question: Did Christ suffer bodily pain only?
before.answer: No; His greatest suffering was a fearful anguish of soul on account of our sins
before.right: No; His greatest suffering was a fearful anguish of soul on account of our sins

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 22:44 gives the sweat like drops of blood in the garden, Matthew 26:38 gives "My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death," and Matthew 27:46 gives the cry "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" on the cross.

before.question: When in particular did he suffer this anguish?
before.answer: In the garden, when His sweat became like drops of blood and He said, "My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death"; and on the cross, when He cried, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"
before.right: In the garden of Gethsemane and on the cross, crying "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Isaiah 53:7 says He was led like a lamb to the slaughter and did not open His mouth. The answer's patience is drawn from that silent submission, which the verse pictures.

before.question: How did Christ act through all this suffering?
before.answer: He was patient as a lamb that is led to the slaughter
before.right: He was patient as a lamb that is led to the slaughter

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 6:23 names the wages of sin as death, and 1 Peter 2:24 says Christ bore our sins in His body on the tree. Together they teach that His death paid the penalty of sin. No single verse says it outright.

before.question: What did Christ accomplish for us by His death on the cross?
before.answer: By His death He has paid the wages of sin, which is death
before.right: By His death He has paid the wages of sin, which is death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 6:4 says believers were buried with Christ through baptism, but no shown verse says He buried our sins, hallowed our graves, or took away their horror. That comfort is the catechism's own teaching.

before.question: What comfort do we have from the burial of Christ?
before.answer: He has buried our sins, hallowed our graves, and taken away their horror
before.right: He has buried our sins, hallowed our graves, and taken away their horror

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Philippians 2:9 says that therefore God exalted Christ to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names, matching the answer.

before.question: According to Philippians 2:9, what did God do for Christ after He humbled Himself and became obedient to death on a cross?
before.answer: God exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names
before.right: God exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: No shown verse counts steps of Christ's exaltation. The verses describe resurrection, ascension, session at the right hand, and judgment, and Ephesians 4:9 hints at descent, but the five-step grouping is church teaching.

before.question: How many steps do you notice in the exaltation of Christ?
before.answer: Five: His descent into hell; His resurrection; His ascension; His session at the right hand of the Father; His coming to judge the living and the dead
before.right: Five: descent into hell, resurrection, ascension, session at right hand, coming to judge

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Peter 3:19 says Christ went and preached to the spirits in prison, and Hebrews 2:14 says by His death He destroyed the devil. The answer's "victory made known" is a joining of these, not a direct statement.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: No shown verse says the victory was made known during the descent; that link is the catechism's own inference from these two passages.

before.question: What did Christ accomplish when he descended into hell?
before.answer: He made known the victory which He had won over the devil, and preached to the spirits in prison
before.right: He made known His victory over the devil and preached to the spirits in prison

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 1:4 says Christ was declared Son of God by His resurrection, Romans 4:25 says He was raised for our justification, and Romans 6:9 says death no longer has dominion over Him.

before.question: What benefit do we have from the resurrection of Christ?
before.answer: 1. The resurrection assures us that Christ is the Son of God, and that He has conquered death and fully satisfied for our sins
before.right: Assures us Christ is God's Son, conquered death, and satisfied for our sins

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 1:9 says Jesus was taken up and a cloud hid Him from sight, Luke 24:26 speaks of Him entering His glory, and John 14:2 says He goes to prepare a place in the Father's house.

before.question: What is meant by the ascension of Christ?
before.answer: He left the earth, so that He is no longer visibly present, and He entered into His Father's glory to prepare a place for us in the Father's house
before.right: He left the earth, no longer visibly present, and entered the Father's glory to prepare a place for us

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Colossians 3:1-2 tells believers, with Christ seated at God's right hand, to set their minds on things above. Philippians 1:23 has Paul desiring to depart and be with Christ.

before.question: What does the ascension of Christ teach us?
before.answer: It teaches us to be heavenly-minded, and to have a desire to depart and be with Christ
before.right: It teaches us to be heavenly-minded, and to have a desire to depart and be with Christ

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The verses show the Son of Man coming in glory to judge all nations, the Lord descending from heaven, and Christ appointed to judge the living and the dead. The exact phrase "last day" is not in these verses.

before.question: When will He again come to earth in a visible manner?
before.answer: On the last day, when He comes to judge the living and the dead
before.right: On the last day, when He comes to judge the living and the dead

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 12:48 says that the word Christ has spoken will judge the one who rejects Him on the last day, so His Word is the rule of judgment.

before.question: By what rule will Christ judge us?
before.answer: He will judge us by His Word
before.right: He will judge us by His Word

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Isaiah 42:17 describes those who trust in idols and call molten images their gods; Psalm 31:6 sets clinging to idols against trusting the LORD. Scripture teaches that trust placed in what is not God is idolatry.

before.question: What is meant by an idol?
before.answer: Anything that man worships, fears, loves, and trusts in instead of the one true God
before.right: Anything that man worships, fears, loves, and trusts instead of the true God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: No shown verse lists these four works together. Acts 13:2 and John 16:8 show the Spirit calling and convicting, but enlightening, sanctifying, and preserving are not shown. The four-part summary comes from Luther's explanation of the Third Article.

before.question: What is the work of the Holy Spirit?
before.answer: To call, enlighten, sanctify, and preserve
before.right: To call, enlighten, sanctify, and preserve

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 16:8-9 says the Spirit convicts the world concerning sin, because they do not believe in Christ. 2 Thessalonians 2:14 says God calls believers through the gospel to share Christ's glory.

before.question: How does the Holy Spirit call us?
before.answer: The Holy Spirit calls us by awakening in our hearts a deep sense of sin, and by inviting us to accept the grace of God in Christ
before.right: By awakening in our hearts a sense of sin and inviting us to accept God's grace

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Stephen tells the council that they always resist the Holy Spirit, as their fathers did, so not all obey the Spirit's call. The refusal to repent and come to Christ is an extension of that point.

before.question: Do all obey the call of the Holy Spirit?
before.answer: No; many resist the Holy Spirit, and will not repent and come to Christ
before.right: No; many resist the Holy Spirit, and will not repent and come to Christ

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 7:51 says the people "always resist the Holy Spirit," and Hebrews 3:8 warns against hardening hearts when God's voice is heard. Despising and conscience are not stated in these verses.

before.question: When does a person harden his heart?
before.answer: A person hardens his heart when he persistently despises and opposes the voice of the Holy Spirit in his conscience
before.right: A person hardens his heart when he persistently despises and opposes the voice of the Holy Spirit in his conscience

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Peter calls the hearers to repent for forgiveness (Acts 2:38), and Romans 10:9 ties salvation to believing in the heart that God raised Jesus; the answer's pairing of repentance and belief follows from these.

before.question: Who obey the call of the Holy Spirit?
before.answer: They who repent of their sins and believe the Gospel
before.right: They who repent of their sins and believe the Gospel

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The prodigal confesses his sin and unworthiness, Paul describes godly sorrow leading to repentance, David confesses his sin to the LORD, and Hosea asks God to take away iniquity and receive them graciously.

before.question: What is it to repent?
before.answer: He who truly repents, feels his sins with shame and sorrow, he freely confesses his sins to God, and earnestly seeks the grace of God in Christ
before.right: To feel sins with shame and sorrow, confess them to God, and seek His grace

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 1:17 says grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. First Corinthians 2:12 says we received the Spirit from God so that we may understand what God has freely given us. Together they teach the answer.

before.question: How do we learn that the grace of God is found in Christ?
before.answer: We learn this through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit
before.right: We learn this through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul asks that the eyes of the believers' hearts be enlightened so they may know God's gifts, and says we received the Spirit so we may understand what God has freely given us.

before.question: What is meant by the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit?
before.answer: Through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit our knowledge of the Gospel truths becomes a living and saving knowledge to our hearts
before.right: Our knowledge of Gospel truths becomes living and saving knowledge in our hearts

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 3 says righteousness comes through faith in Jesus Christ, and a man is justified by faith apart from works. Acts 26:18 adds turning from Satan's power to God and forgiveness through faith; Romans 8:2 adds freedom from sin and death.

before.question: What is the true and living faith in Jesus Christ?
before.answer: This is faith, that a repentant sinner lays hold of Christ as his only Savior from sin, and death, and the power of Satan
before.right: A repentant sinner lays hold of Christ as his only Savior from sin, death, and Satan

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 1:25 says people worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, and Deuteronomy 17:3 names going to worship the sun, moon, and host of heaven. Images, angels, and saints are applications the verses only partly cover.

before.question: Who practice idolatry openly?
before.answer: They who worship the created things instead of the Creator, and pray to the sun, the moon, stars, images, angels, or saints
before.right: Those who worship creation instead of Creator and pray to images, angels, saints

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 5:31-32 says Christ came to call sinners to repentance, and Romans 3:22-24 says all believers are justified freely by grace. No shown verse says only those who bitterly feel their sin can receive faith.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The answer's "only" and "bitterly feels the pain and misery" go beyond the verses shown. Romans 3:22 says there is "no distinction" among those who believe, which does not limit faith to the bitterly contrite.

before.question: Can only a repentant sinner have this faith in Christ?
before.answer: Yes; the faith which lays hold of Christ and His righteousness, can be wrought in that heart only which bitterly feels the pain and misery of living in sin
before.right: Yes; faith in Christ can be wrought only in a heart that bitterly feels the pain of living in sin

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The father's weak but sincere cry, "I do believe; help my unbelief," is answered by Jesus, who then casts out the spirit (9:25), so Christ accepts such faith.

before.question: Does God accept this weak faith?
before.answer: Yes, indeed; only it be true and sincere
before.right: Yes, indeed; only it be true and sincere

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 2:4 says God acts "because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy," so love and mercy are what move Him. The verse does not say "everlasting" or "alone."

before.question: What moves God to forgive sin so freely?
before.answer: His everlasting love and mercy alone
before.right: His everlasting love and mercy alone

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Forgiveness comes "in Him" through His blood (Eph 1:7); He is the atoning sacrifice for the whole world's sins (1 John 2:2); He bore our sins on the tree (1 Pet 2:24).

before.question: For whose sake does God forgive us our sins?
before.answer: For Christ's sake, who has satisfied for the sins of the whole world by His death on the cross
before.right: For Christ's sake, who has satisfied for the sins of the whole world by His death on the cross

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 5:1-2 gives peace with God and access into grace through faith; Ephesians 1:5 names adoption as sons; Ephesians 1:14 calls the Spirit the pledge of our inheritance. Together these match the answer's blessings.

before.question: To what does the forgiveness of sins necessarily lead?
before.answer: The forgiveness of sins leads to the full enjoyment of the blessed rights which belong to a child of God; it also gives free access to the Father's fellowship and blessing, and to the glorious inheritance of eternal life
before.right: The full enjoyment of a child of God's rights, access to the Father's fellowship, and eternal life

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Titus 3:5 names the new birth as a renewal by the Holy Spirit, and Colossians 3:10 describes the new self being renewed in the image of its Creator. The indwelling wording is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is the New Birth?
before.answer: The New Birth is the gracious work of the Holy Spirit whereby He, through His indwelling in our hearts, renews the image of God in us, and thus creates a new spiritual man
before.right: The Holy Spirit's gracious work renewing God's image in us and creating new spiritual life

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 2 Corinthians 5:17 says one in Christ is a new creation, the new life the answer names. Ezekiel 36:26 states the new heart outright: "I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you."

before.question: What change is wrought in us in the New Birth?
before.answer: We get a new heart or a new spiritual life.
before.right: We get a new heart or a new spiritual life.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 John 4:19 says "We love because He first loved us," so the answer is drawn from it: love answering God's prior love. Verse 4:7 links love with being born of God.

before.question: In what does this new life really consist?
before.answer: It consists in love to God who first loved us.
before.right: It consists in love to God who first loved us.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 3:5 names water and the Spirit as the means of new birth, and 1 Peter 1:23 says we are born again through the living word of God. The verses do not limit these to little children or to those who fell away.

before.question: By what means is the New Birth accomplished?
before.answer: In little children it is accomplished by water and the Spirit in baptism; but in those who have fallen from the grace of their baptism, also by the Word of God
before.right: In children by water and Spirit in baptism; in others by the Word of God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus says that no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again, so the new birth is necessary. John 3:5 says the same about entering the kingdom.

before.question: Is the New Birth necessary to our salvation?
before.answer: Yes, indeed; no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.
before.right: Yes, no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 31:6 sets clinging to worthless idols against trusting the LORD, and 2 Kings 17:9 says the Israelites secretly did wrong against the LORD by building high places.

before.question: Who practice idolatry secretly?
before.answer: They who turn their love, fear, and trust from the living God, that they may secretly cling to something else than Him
before.right: Those who inwardly turn their love, fear, and trust from God to something else

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 2 Thessalonians 2:13 names the Spirit's sanctification of believers. Philippians 1:6 says God will carry on the good work He began to completion, which supports preservation.

before.question: What does the Holy Spirit further work in the believer?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Colossians 3:9-10 describes putting off the old self with its practices and putting on the new self, which is being renewed. The ongoing "being renewed" supports the answer's "more and more" wording.

before.question: How is the daily renewal accomplished?
before.answer: The old man, or sin, is put away more and more, and the new man, or the new spiritual life, appears more and more in all our conduct
before.right: The old man and sin are put away more and more; the new spiritual life appears in our conduct

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Scripture does not name the Spirit as the sole keeper, but it teaches the answer: 2 Timothy 1:14 has the Spirit helping believers guard the faith, and 1 Peter 1:5 and Philippians 1:6 promise they are kept to the end.

before.question: What is the work of Preservation done by the Holy Spirit?
before.answer: Preservation is the gracious work of the Holy Spirit whereby He keeps us, through all temptations, in the true and living faith in Jesus, until the end
before.right: The Holy Spirit's gracious work keeping us in true faith through all temptations until the end

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 14:26 says the Holy Spirit will teach and remind believers, and Romans 8:14 says those led by the Spirit are sons of God, which supports teaching and guiding. Correction is not stated in the shown verses; comfort is only indirectly supported by John 14:27 and Romans 8:15.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The shown verses clearly support teaching and guiding, but nothing shown says the Spirit corrects the believer, and comfort rests only on indirect passages.

before.question: How does the Holy Spirit preserve the believer?
before.answer: He teaches and guides, corrects and comforts him
before.right: He teaches and guides, corrects and comforts him

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 2:42 shows believers devoted to the apostles' teaching and the breaking of bread in fellowship, and Ephesians 1:22-23 calls the church Christ's body. The catechism answer is drawn from these.

before.question: What is the holy Christian church?
before.answer: The holy Christian Church is the congregation of saints or true believers, where the Word of God is preached and the sacraments are administered according to the ordinance of God
before.right: The congregation of saints and true believers where God's Word is preached and sacraments administered

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The verses say God's Spirit dwells in believers, making them God's holy temple (1 Cor 3:16-17). Christ sanctifies the church by His word (Eph 5:26). The sinful Corinthian church is still called holy (1 Cor 1:2).

before.question: Why is the church called holy?
before.answer: The church is called holy because of the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, who performs His sanctifying work in all its members. For this reason the church is called holy, in spite of its sins and shortcomings
before.right: Because the Holy Spirit indwells it and sanctifies its members, despite their sins and shortcomings

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 28:19 commands making disciples of all nations, and Revelation 5:9 pictures people from every tribe, tongue, people, and nation. Matthew 28:20's "always, to the end of the age" supports the all-times part.

before.question: Why is the church called universal?
before.answer: The church is called universal because its object is to gather all nations, and because it includes all true believers of all times and all places
before.right: Its object is to gather all nations and include all true believers of all times and places

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Scripture never uses the word "militant," but Ephesians 6:12 says believers' struggle is against spiritual forces of evil, and 1 Peter 2:11 says fleshly desires war against the soul while they live as exiles on earth.

before.question: What is the state of the church on earth?
before.answer: The church of God on earth is militant
before.right: The church of God on earth is militant

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 13:39 names the devil as the enemy, Galatians 5:17 and 1 John 2:16 set the flesh and the world against God's Spirit and Father, and 1 Corinthians 15:26 states that death is the last enemy.

before.question: Who are the enemies of the church?
before.answer: The enemies of the church are the devil, the world, and our own flesh. Its last enemy is death
before.right: The enemies of the church are the devil, the world, and our own flesh. Its last enemy is death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The redeemed stand before the throne holding palm branches, and death, mourning, crying and pain are gone; Christ puts all enemies under His feet, and death is the last one destroyed.

before.question: What will be the state of the church in heaven?
before.answer: It will be triumphant, because all its enemies are conquered
before.right: It will be triumphant, because all its enemies are conquered

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Pagan sacrifices are offered to demons (1 Cor 10:20), Jesus calls the devil the father of lies (John 8:44), and whoever practices sin is of the devil (1 John 3:8).

before.question: Whom do all idolaters really serve?
before.answer: They serve the devil who is the father of lies, and the lord of all impenitent and hardened sinners
before.right: They serve the devil, father of lies and lord of hardened sinners

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Cor 12:27 calls the believers gathered there "the body of Christ," and 1 Tim 3:15 calls God's household "the church of the living God." The answer's claim that the church is in the congregation follows from these.

before.question: Is the holy Christian church found in this place?
before.answer: Yes; in the congregation, which in Scripture is called the body of Christ and the household of God.
before.right: Yes; in the congregation, called in Scripture the body of Christ and the household of God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus gives the power to forgive or withhold forgiveness of sins to His disciples. The verse names the disciples, not the congregation; the congregation-through-ministers wording is the catechism's application of it.

before.question: Whom has God given power to declare the forgiveness of sins?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The verses show confessing to God (Psalm 32:5; 1 John 1:9) and to one another (James 5:16), but name no pastor and give no ordering. The pastor step is church teaching.

before.question: To whom should a repentant Christian confess his sins?
before.answer: First of all to God; then, if he feels the need of it, to his pastor; finally to his neighbor, if he feels that he has wronged him in any way
before.right: First to God; if needed, to his pastor; to his neighbor if he wronged him

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul says that at the last trumpet, when the Lord comes, the dead will be raised imperishable and the dead in Christ will rise first. The verses do not spell out reunion with the soul.

before.question: What is the resurrection of the body?
before.answer: On the last day, when the Lord Jesus returns to earth, the bodies of the dead shall be made alive and shall be reunited with their souls
before.right: When Christ returns, the dead's bodies will be made alive and reunited with their souls

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 25:46 says the righteous go into eternal life and the condemned into eternal punishment; Revelation 20:15 says those not written in the Book of Life are thrown into the lake of fire.

before.question: Where do all the risen go after the day of judgment?
before.answer: The chosen enter into life everlasting; the condemned, into eternal death
before.right: The chosen enter into life everlasting; the condemned, into eternal death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: God dwells with His people, wipes away every tear, and there is no more death, mourning, crying, or pain; they worship Him, see His face, and reign forever. The holy angels are not named in these verses.

before.question: What is life everlasting?
before.answer: Life everlasting is the blessed state in which the chosen are free from all evil, and live forever in fellowship with their God and Savior, praising God in the company of the holy angels, in everlasting peace and joy
before.right: The blessed state where the chosen are free from evil and live forever in fellowship with God and holy angels

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Revelation 20:14 calls the lake of fire the second death, and Matthew 25:41 names eternal fire. Second Thessalonians 1:9 adds that the lost suffer eternal destruction, separated from the Lord's presence.

before.question: What is eternal death?
before.answer: Eternal death is a dreadful state of separation from God, and everlasting anguish and suffering in hell
before.right: A dreadful state of separation from God and everlasting anguish and suffering in hell

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John 3:18 says whoever does not believe is condemned, and Rev 20:15 says those not written in the Book of Life are cast into the lake of fire. Luke 13:5 adds that those who do not repent will perish.

before.question: Who will be condemned on the Last Day?
before.answer: All who continue in impenitence and unbelief until death
before.right: All who continue in impenitence and unbelief until death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Revelation 2:10 says, "Be faithful even unto death, and I will give you the crown of life," which matches the answer's steadfastness until death. The question's reference verses say only that believers have eternal life.

before.question: Who obtain life everlasting?
before.answer: All who continue steadfast in faith until death
before.right: All who continue steadfast in faith until death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul tells Timothy that the Holy Scriptures are able to make him wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus, so the answer that God shows salvation in them is stated directly.

before.question: Where does God show us how we may be saved?
before.answer: In the holy Scriptures, also called the Bible
before.right: In the holy Scriptures, also called the Bible

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul says all God's promises are "Yes" in Christ, so our "Amen" is spoken through Him. The Amen affirms God's sure promises, though the verse does not state the speaker's personal certainty.

before.question: Why do you end your confession of faith with the word Amen?
before.answer: Because I know that what I here confess is certainly true
before.right: Because I know that what I here confess is certainly true

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus says, "If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it," so the answer, praying in the name of Jesus, is stated directly in the question's reference.

before.question: In whose name must we pray?
before.answer: We must pray in the name of Jesus
before.right: We must pray in the name of Jesus

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul says "Pray without ceasing" (1 Thess 5:17) and "Pray in the Spirit at all times" (Eph 6:18), which teach constant prayer. The places and occasions part follows from "at all times."

before.question: When should we pray?
before.answer: The attitude of our hearts should be one of constant prayer, and our communion with God should not be confined to certain times and places, but we should speak with Him whenever we feel the need of it
before.right: Our hearts should be in constant prayer; we should speak with God whenever we feel the need

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul urges that prayers be offered for everyone (1 Tim 2:1), and Jesus says to pray for those who persecute you (Matt 5:44), which covers enemies.

before.question: For whom should we pray?
before.answer: We should pray not only for ourselves, but also for others,--even our enemies
before.right: We should pray for ourselves and for others, even our enemies

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul prays that believers be filled with knowledge of God's will and spiritual wisdom (Col 1:9-10), and Phil 4:6 says to bring requests to God in everything, which supports praying for other gifts too.

before.question: For what should we pray?
before.answer: First of all we should pray for the spiritual gifts necessary to our salvation; but we may also pray for other gifts, both spiritual and temporal
before.right: First for spiritual gifts necessary to salvation; also for other spiritual and temporal gifts

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 8:26 says the Spirit helps us in our weakness, since we do not know how to pray, and intercedes for us. Zechariah 12:10 speaks of "a spirit of grace and prayer" poured out by God.

before.question: Who teaches us to pray well?
before.answer: The Holy Spirit, who is also called the Spirit of prayer
before.right: The Holy Spirit, who is also called the Spirit of prayer

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:9-13 gives the prayer Jesus taught His disciples, introduced as "this is how you should pray." The verses do not call it the most perfect prayer; that judgment is the catechism's own.

before.question: Which is the most perfect prayer?
before.answer: The most perfect prayer is the Lord's Prayer, which Christ taught His own disciples.
before.right: The most perfect prayer is the Lord's Prayer, which Christ taught His own disciples

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Galatians 3:26 says believers are sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus. Romans 8:15 contrasts the spirit of fear with the Spirit of sonship, by whom we cry "Abba! Father!"

before.question: Who alone can confidently call God Father?
before.answer: Believers in Christ, who are God's children through faith
before.right: Believers in Christ, who are God's children through faith

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The LORD contrasts outward appearance, which man sees, with the heart, which the LORD sees. The answer's "attitude of our hearts toward Him" is a fuller statement of "the heart."

before.question: Upon what does God really look?
before.answer: Upon the attitude of our hearts toward Him
before.right: Upon the attitude of our hearts toward Him

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:9 asks that God's name be hallowed but does not say when. The Word-taught-purely and holy-life link is Luther's explanation of the petition; Colossians 3:16 and 1 Thessalonians 4:7 touch its parts without stating it.

before.question: When is the name of God hallowed among us?
before.answer: When the Word of God is taught in its truth and purity, and we, as children of God, lead holy lives according to it
before.right: When God's Word is taught purely and we lead holy lives by it

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 12:8 says whoever confesses Christ before men is confessed before the angels, matching the confession part. Leviticus 22:31-32 ties keeping God's commandments to not profaning His holy name and being acknowledged as holy, matching the holy-life part.

before.question: When do we hallow the name of God among our fellow men?
before.answer: We hallow the name of God when we freely confess it before men in accordance with the Word, and when we as God's children live holy lives in obedience to the Word
before.right: When we confess God's name before men and live holy lives according to His Word

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 2:24 shows that a life contrary to God's law causes His name to be blasphemed. Ezekiel 22:26 shows that priests who do violence to His law profane His holy things and so profane Him.

before.question: Who profanes the name of God?
before.answer: He that teaches and lives otherwise than the Word of God teaches, profanes the name of God
before.right: He that teaches and lives otherwise than the Word of God teaches, profanes the name of God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:10 asks that the kingdom come, and Luke 17:21 and Matthew 12:28 say it is among or upon people, but no shown verse says we become partakers. That gloss is the catechism's reading of the petition.

before.question: What is meant by saying that the kingdom of God comes to us?
before.answer: It means that we become partakers in it
before.right: It means that we become partakers in it

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The Father gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask (Luke 11:13), and where the Spirit of God works the kingdom of God has come upon you (Matt 12:28). Matt 6:10 is only a prayer for it to come.

before.question: When does the kingdom of God come to us?
before.answer: The kingdom of God comes to us when our heavenly Father gives us His Holy Spirit, so that by His grace we believe His holy Word and live a godly life here in time and hereafter in eternity.
before.right: When the Father gives us His Holy Spirit, so we believe His Word and live a godly life

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: No shown verse says this is God's will. Psalm 145:21 and Revelation 5:13 show creatures praising God forever, and 1 Thessalonians 3:13 mentions holiness, but none names happiness or defines God's will this way.

before.question: What is the will of God?
before.answer: It is the will of God that all His rational creatures should praise Him forever in perfect holiness and happiness
before.right: It is the will of God that all His rational creatures should praise Him forever in perfect holiness and happiness

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Proverbs 14:2 ties fearing the LORD to walking in uprightness rather than devious ways, and Psalm 89:7 shows God as greatly feared and awesome above all, matching the high regard in the answer.

before.question: When do we fear God?
before.answer: We fear God when we think so highly of Him, that we are afraid of offending Him by any wrongdoing
before.right: We fear God when we think so highly of Him we fear offending Him

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:10 places God's will being done in heaven, and Psalm 103:20-21 shows the angels blessing the LORD and doing His will. "Undisturbed peace and joy" is expanded from Luke 2:14 and 15:10.

before.question: Where is the will of God done in this manner?
before.answer: In heaven, where the holy angels praise God in undisturbed peace and joy
before.right: In heaven, where the holy angels praise God in peace and joy

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 33:10 says the LORD frustrates the plans of the nations and thwarts their devices; Philippians 2:13 says God works in us to will and to act. Together they teach the answer's two parts.

before.question: When is the will of God done among us, as it is in heaven?
before.answer: When God brings to nothing all evil plans and purposes that would hinder the hallowing of His name and the coming of His kingdom, and when God strengthens us and keeps us steadfast in His Word and in faith, until death
before.right: When God brings evil plans to nothing and strengthens us to remain steadfast in His Word until death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Philippians 2:13 says God works in us to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose, so God Himself helps us do His will. The "merciful and faithful" wording echoes 1 Cor 1:9 and 2 Cor 4:1.

before.question: Who will help us to do the will of God?
before.answer: God, who is merciful and faithful, will Himself help us to do His will
before.right: God, who is merciful and faithful, will Himself help us to do His will

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:25 names food, drink, and clothing as the needs we should not worry about, since God cares for them. Home and property are not named in the shown verses; that part follows Luther's wider explanation.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The answer's full list, including home and property, goes somewhat beyond what the shown verses say, though food and clothing are supported.

before.question: What is meant by daily bread?
before.answer: By daily bread is meant all those things which are needed for our support and well-being in life, as food and clothing, home and property, etc
before.right: All things needed for our support and well-being in life: food, clothing, home, and property

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:11 asks God for our daily bread, and Hebrews 13:5 tells us to be content with what we have. Together they teach contentment with what God daily provides.

before.question: Of what does the word "daily" remind you?
before.answer: I must be content with that which God gives me
before.right: I must be content with that which God gives me

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:34 forbids worrying about tomorrow and says today has enough trouble of its own, which is the lesson the answer draws from "this day." The verse does not mention the Lord's Prayer.

before.question: Why are the words "this day" added?
before.answer: They are added that I should not be anxious for tomorrow, but let each day bear its own burdens
before.right: They are added that I should not be anxious for tomorrow, but let each day bear its own burdens

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 5:45 says God sends sun and rain on the evil and the unrighteous as well as the good, so He gives daily gifts to the wicked too. The verses shown do not say they receive without thanksgiving or miss His blessing.

before.question: Does God give daily bread to those only who pray for it?
before.answer: No; He gives daily bread also to the wicked, but they receive it without thanksgiving, and miss His blessing
before.right: No; He gives daily bread also to the wicked, but they receive it without thanksgiving, and miss His blessing

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:11 teaches asking God for our daily bread, and 1 Thessalonians 5:18 teaches giving thanks in every circumstance. Asking for the blessing is implied rather than stated.

before.question: How should the children of God receive their daily bread?
before.answer: They should ask God to bless their daily bread, and return Him thanks for it
before.right: They should ask God to bless their daily bread and return Him thanks for it

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: No shown verse counts kinds of the fear of God. Job 31:23 shows terror at God's calamity and Psalm 103:13 shows fear as a child's relation to a father, but neither says there are two kinds.

before.question: Of how many kinds is the fear of God?
before.answer: Of two kinds: slavish fear and child-like fear
before.right: Of two kinds: slavish fear and child-like fear

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 6:12 asks God to "forgive us our debts," treating sins as debts owed to God. The answer's guilt-or-debt idea follows from that wording; the "brought upon ourselves" part is the catechism's gloss.

before.question: What is implied by the word "trespasses"?
before.answer: Thereby is implied our guilt or debt to God, which we have brought upon ourselves by our sins
before.right: Thereby is implied our guilt or debt to God, which we have brought upon ourselves by our sins

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 1:7 says that in Christ we have redemption through His blood and the forgiveness of our trespasses, and 1 John 1:7 says His blood cleanses us from all sin. The answer follows from these.

before.question: Can we feel assured that God will forgive us this debt?
before.answer: Yes; Jesus Christ has paid for all our sins
before.right: Yes; Jesus Christ has paid for all our sins

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 John 1:8 says believers who claim to have no sin deceive themselves, and 1:9 pairs confession with forgiveness. Together they teach that Christians sin and always need forgiveness; "every day" is implied, not stated.

before.question: Why must the believer ask the forgiveness of sins every day?
before.answer: Because he sins every day, and is always in need of forgiveness
before.right: Because he sins every day, and is always in need of forgiveness

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Daniel says the petitions are not presented because of our righteous acts but because of God's great compassion, so we confess we deserve nothing and ask for mercy.

before.question: What do we confess to God in this petition?
before.answer: We confess that we are not worthy of the least of that which we ask, neither have we deserved it; but we pray that He would give it to us out of His mercy
before.right: We confess we are unworthy of God's mercy, yet pray He will grant our requests out of His mercy

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: James 1:14 describes temptation as a person being lured away and enticed by his own evil desires, which matches the answer's idea of enticements that invite to sin.

before.question: What is meant by temptation?
before.answer: By temptation is meant opportunities that invite to sin
before.right: By temptation is meant opportunities that invite to sin

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: James 1:3 says the testing of faith develops perseverance, and Deuteronomy 13:3 says God tests His people to learn whether they love Him, which together match the answer's trying, faith, patience, and love.

before.question: Why then does God permit us to be tempted?
before.answer: God permits us to be tempted in order to try us, and in order that it may be seen whether we have true faith, love, and patience
before.right: To try us and show whether we have faith, love, and patience

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 2:2-3 names the three sources: the ruler of the power of the air and the spirit at work in disobedient people (the devil), the ways of this world, and the cravings of our flesh. Paul does not use the word "tempt" here.

before.question: Who, on the other hand, tempt us to sin?
before.answer: The devil, the world, and our own flesh, tempt us to sin
before.right: The devil, the world, and our own flesh, tempt us to sin

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul says Eve was deceived by the serpent's cunning and fears the Corinthians' minds may be led astray, so the devil works on the mind. The verse does not use the catechism's exact wording.

before.question: How does the devil tempt us?
before.answer: The devil tempts us by putting evil thoughts into our minds
before.right: The devil tempts us by putting evil thoughts into our minds

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Threats appear in Acts 4:21, enticing words in 2 Peter 2:18, and bad example in 1 Corinthians 10:6-7. Together they teach the three parts of the answer, though not as one explicit statement.

before.question: How does the world tempt us?
before.answer: The world tempts us by threats, attractive invitations, and bad example
before.right: The world tempts us by threats, attractive invitations, and bad example

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 John 4:18 says fear involves punishment and is driven out by perfect love, so the answer, fearing God out of dread of punishment, follows from the verse. The phrase "slavish fear" itself does not appear.

before.question: What is meant by slavish fear?
before.answer: When we fear God because we are afraid of punishment
before.right: When we fear God because we are afraid of punishment

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: James 1:14 says each person is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed, which matches the answer that our own flesh tempts by its evil desires.

before.question: How does our flesh tempt us?
before.answer: Our own flesh tempts by its evil desires
before.right: Our own flesh tempts by its evil desires

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: James says trials come "when you encounter" them and that testing develops perseverance so we may be mature; 1 Corinthians 10:13 says every temptation is common to man. Together they teach the answer.

before.question: Can we ever be free from temptations in this world?
before.answer: No; the conditions of this present life are such that temptations must follow, and we need them for our bringing up in the kingdom of God
before.right: No; temptations must follow in this life, and we need them for our growth in God's kingdom

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 6:17 names the word of God as the sword of the Spirit, and Matthew 26:41 tells us to watch and pray so we do not enter into temptation. Avoiding the invitation to temptation is only implied there.

before.question: What are our weapons against temptation?
before.answer: We must use the Word of God, watch and pray, and take care not to invite temptation
before.right: Use God's Word, watch and pray, and take care not to invite temptation

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: John says the confidence we have before God is that He hears us when we ask according to His will, so we know our requests are heard. The verses do not mention Amen itself.

before.question: Why is this word added?
before.answer: It is added in order that I may be fully assured that these petitions are acceptable to our Father in heaven, and are heard by Him
before.right: It is added that I may be assured these petitions are acceptable to God and are heard by Him

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 7:7-8 commands us to ask and promises that it will be given, and Psalm 50:15 says "Call upon Me... I will deliver you." The gloss that Amen means "surely; so be it" is a word meaning not stated in these verses.

before.question: How can I feel assured of this?
