before.answer: God Himself has commanded us to pray and has promised to hear us. Amen, Amen means: Surely; so be it.
before.right: God has commanded us to pray and promised to hear us; Amen means "so be it"

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul asked three times for the thorn to be removed, and the Lord answered with His grace and power instead. Ephesians 3:20 says God can do far more than we ask or imagine.

before.question: Does God always answer our prayer as we desire?
before.answer: No; He often answers our prayer by giving us something else and something better than we ask or think
before.right: No; He often gives us something else and something better than we ask or think

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 John 5:3 says the love of God is keeping His commandments, and Genesis 22:12 shows fear of God as not withholding what He asks, so the answer follows from these verses.

before.question: What is meant by child-like fear?
before.answer: When we love God so dearly that we wish to do nothing that is against His will
before.right: When we love God so dearly that we wish to do nothing against His will

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 18:7-8 says God will bring about justice for His elect who cry to Him, asking whether He will keep deferring their help, and that He will act promptly. The parable teaches persistent prayer, so answers can come after waiting.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: Luke 18:8 says God will act promptly, and these verses do not state that His delay is meant to strengthen faith, so that purpose is an inference.

before.question: Does God answer our prayer at once?
before.answer: Sometimes; but He often delays His answer in order to strengthen our faith and our hope
before.right: Sometimes; but He often delays His answer to strengthen our faith and our hope

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Christ's command in Matthew 28:19 is to go, make disciples of all nations, and baptize them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, which is the last chapter of Matthew the answer names.

before.question: What is God's command concerning Baptism?
before.answer: It is given in the words of Christ in the last chapter of Matthew
before.right: It is given in the words of Christ in the last chapter of Matthew

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 28:19 states that disciples are to be baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, matching the printed answer.

before.question: In whose name then are you baptized?
before.answer: I am baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
before.right: I am baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses record baptisms by Peter, John, Paul, and Jesus's disciples, but none states who should administer baptism, or a rule for ministers versus any Christian in necessity. That rule is church teaching.

before.question: Who should administer Baptism?
before.answer: Baptism should be administered by the minister of the church, but when necessary it may be administered by any Christian
before.right: Baptism should be administered by the church minister, but when necessary by any Christian

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 2:38 links baptism with forgiveness of sins, Titus 3:5 and 1 Peter 3:21 say baptism saves, and Romans 6:4 speaks of union with Christ's death and resurrection, giving new life.

before.question: What benefit do we have from Baptism?
before.answer: Baptism works the forgiveness of sins, delivers from death and the devil, and gives everlasting life to all who believe what the Word and promise of God declare
before.right: Baptism works forgiveness of sins, delivers from death and the devil, and gives everlasting life to believers

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Mark 16:16 states the promise: "Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved," which is the passage the answer names as the place where God's promise is given.

before.question: What is God's promise concerning Baptism?
before.answer: It is given in the words of Christ in the sixteenth chapter of Mark
before.right: It is given in the words of Christ in the sixteenth chapter of Mark

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 6:3-5 says those baptized into Christ Jesus are baptized into His death and united with Him in His resurrection, which teaches the fellowship with Christ the answer names. The verses do not explicitly mention the devil or deliverance from death.

before.question: How does Baptism save us from sin, death, and the devil?
before.answer: In Baptism we come into fellowship with Christ, and are made partakers in His redemption
before.right: In Baptism we come into fellowship with Christ, and are made partakers in His redemption

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Titus 3:5 says God saves through the washing of new birth, not by our works, and Romans 10:17 says faith comes by hearing the word of Christ; the Word-in-the-water wording is the catechism's reading of these.

before.question: How can water do such great things?
before.answer: It is not water indeed that does it, but the Word of God, which is in and with the water, and faith which trusts this Word of God in the water
before.right: Not water, but the Word of God in and with the water, and faith trusting this Word

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: No shown verse says only God's children fear Him this way. Psalm 103:13 and Proverbs 14:26 link fearers with God's compassion and their children, while Psalm 34:11 invites children to learn the fear of the LORD.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The shown verses do not say "only" God's children fear Him this way; Psalm 34:11 and Deuteronomy 31:13 call others, including children who do not yet know the law, to learn that fear.

before.question: Who fear God in this manner?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Scripture never calls Baptism a covenant. Romans 6:4 speaks of being buried with Christ through baptism and walking in newness of life, but the covenant label and the renunciation vows come from church teaching.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: No shown verse calls Baptism a covenant or mentions renouncing the devil, so the answer's "Yes" rests on church teaching rather than these passages.

before.question: Is not Baptism also called a covenant?
before.answer: Yes; Baptism is a covenant; in Baptism God gives us a new life and His grace, and we promise Him to renounce the devil and all his works and all his ways, and to believe in the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
before.right: Yes; God gives us new life and grace; we promise to renounce the devil and believe in the Trinity

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Mark 16:16 says whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, so the baptized who keep believing are the ones who receive the promised blessing. The phrase "remain in the covenant" is the catechism's wording, not the verse's.

before.question: Who enjoy the blessings that God promises in Baptism?
before.answer: All who remain in the covenant of their Baptism
before.right: All who remain in the covenant of their Baptism

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 11:22 speaks of "continu[ing] in His kindness," which assumes it is possible to remain in God's kindness, and the kindness is God's gift. It does not mention Baptism.

before.question: Is it possible to remain in the covenant of Baptism?
before.answer: Yes; by the grace of God it is possible
before.right: Yes; by the grace of God it is possible

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 6:17-18 urges prayer and names the word of God, but no shown verse mentions the Lord's Supper or ties these to remaining in baptismal grace. The answer is Lutheran teaching on the means of grace.

before.question: What must we do to remain in the grace of our Baptism?
before.answer: We must watch and pray, and make diligent use of the Word of God and the Lord's Supper
before.right: We must watch and pray, and make diligent use of the Word of God and the Lord's Supper

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses say covenant-breaking is unfaithfulness, and Psalm 78:10-11 mentions forgetting God's deeds, but none names resisting the Spirit, neglecting prayer, or growing worldly-minded. The answer is catechism teaching beyond these verses.

before.question: Which is one way we may break the covenant of our Baptism?
before.answer: When we little by little forget our covenant, resist the Holy Spirit, and neglect prayer, so that we become more and more worldly-minded
before.right: When we little by little forget our covenant, resist the Holy Spirit, and neglect prayer

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Isaiah 55:6-7 bids the sinner seek and call on the LORD and return to Him, with the assurance that He will freely pardon, which matches both parts of the answer: the invitation and prayer.

before.question: How does a repentant sinner get courage to return to God?
before.answer: He gets courage from considering the tender Gospel invitation of Christ, and from seeking God in prayer
before.right: He gets courage from considering the tender Gospel invitation of Christ, and from seeking God in prayer

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 6:3-6 says baptism buries us with Christ into death, our old self was crucified with Him, and we walk in newness of life. The answer's dying and rising imagery follows from this; "daily sorrow and repentance" is Luther's gloss, not stated in the verses.

before.question: What does the baptizing with water signify?
before.answer: It signifies that the old man in us should, by daily sorrow and repentance, be drowned and die, with all sins and evil desires; and again a new man daily appear more and more, who shall live before God in righteousness and purity forever
before.right: The old man should be drowned by repentance with all sins; a new man shall live in righteousness forever

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: None of the shown verses speaks of sponsors or their duties. Acts 8:15 and Ephesians 6:1 concern prayer for new believers and children's obedience, so the answer comes from Lutheran catechism teaching.

before.question: What are the duties of sponsors?
before.answer: They should pray for the child whose baptism they have witnessed, they should remember the covenant of their own Baptism, and afterwards, as far as possible, see that the child is brought up in the fear of God
before.right: Pray for the child, remember own Baptism, and help raise the child in fear of God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The answer is the catechism's own gloss on the First Commandment. 1 John 5:3 supports only the part about keeping God's commandments; the shown verses do not say God is dearer than all else or that joy is found only in Him.

before.question: When do we love God?
before.answer: We love God when He is dearer to us than all else, so that we have no true joy except in Him, and gladly submit to His will in all things
before.right: God is dearer to us than all, we have joy only in Him, gladly submit to His will

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul says the Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread and gave the supper's words, so the timing is stated. The name "Lord's Supper" is not in these verses.

before.question: When did Jesus institute the Lord's Supper?
before.answer: On the night He was betrayed; it is therefore called the Lord's Supper
before.right: On the night He was betrayed; it is therefore called the Lord's Supper

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus says the bread is His body given for you and the cup is the new covenant in His blood. The "in and with" wording goes beyond these verses.

before.question: What do we receive in the Lord's Supper?
before.answer: In and with the bread and the wine we receive the body and blood of Christ, which He gave up in death for us
before.right: In and with the bread and the wine we receive the body and blood of Christ, which He gave up in death for us

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 26:26 records Jesus giving the bread to the disciples and saying, "Take and eat; this is My body," which is the exact words the answer quotes.

before.question: How do you know this?
before.answer: Christ says concerning the bread: "Take and eat; this is My body."
before.right: Christ says concerning the bread: "Take and eat; this is My body."

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 22:20 calls the cup "the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you," and Hebrews 8:8 has God saying He will make the new covenant. Together they teach the answer's point that God made it and it is sealed by Jesus' blood.

before.question: When Jesus says of the cup, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood," what is meant by the new covenant?
before.answer: It is the new covenant which God has made and sealed with the blood of Jesus.
before.right: The new covenant which God made and sealed with the blood of Jesus

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Corinthians 11:28-29 requires each person to examine himself and recognize the Lord's body before eating, which presupposes faith and understanding. The phrase "of age" is not stated in these verses.

before.question: For whom is the Lord's Supper intended?
before.answer: The Lord's Supper is intended for true Christians, who are of age and understanding to examine themselves
before.right: The Lord's Supper is intended for true Christians old enough and understanding enough to examine themselves

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 26:28 says the cup is poured out for the forgiveness of sins, and Luke 1:77 ties salvation to forgiveness, so forgiveness, life, and salvation come together.

before.question: What benefit do we have from the Lord's Supper?
before.answer: It is shown by these words: "Given and shed for you for the forgiveness of sins;" namely, that in the sacrament forgiveness of sins, life, and salvation are given us through these words. For where there is forgiveness of sins, there is also life and salvation.
before.right: Through the words 'Given and shed for you for the forgiveness of sins,' we receive forgiveness, life, and salvation

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The words spoken over the cup, "poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins," and over the bread, "given for you," carry the forgiveness; the verses do not say that believing them is what receives it.

before.question: How can bodily eating and drinking do such great things?
before.answer: It is not the eating and drinking, indeed, that does it, but the words which stand here: "Given and shed for you, for the forgiveness of sins." These words, together with the bodily eating and drinking, are the chief thing in the sacrament; and He that believes these words, has what they say and mean, namely, the forgiveness of sins
before.right: Not the eating and drinking, but the words and faith in them, give forgiveness of sins

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul says eating the Lord's Supper in an unworthy manner brings guilt and judgment, so each must examine himself first. The verses show preparation matters greatly, though they do not compare unworthy partaking with abstaining.

before.question: Is it of little importance how we receive the Lord's Supper?
before.answer: By no means; we must be prepared when we go to partake of these gifts. It is much worse to go to the Lord's Supper unprepared and unworthily than not to go at all
before.right: By no means; we must be prepared to partake of these gifts worthily and not unworthily

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Hebrews 10:22 bids us draw near in full assurance of faith, with hearts cleansed; Matthew 26:28 gives the words of institution, "poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins," which faith receives.

before.question: Who, then, receive this sacrament worthily?
before.answer: Fasting and bodily preparation are indeed a good outward practise, but he is truly worthy and well prepared who has faith in the words "Given and shed for you for the forgiveness of sins."
before.right: Those who have faith in the words "Given and shed for you for the forgiveness of sins"

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Believing from the heart brings justification, and confessing sins brings forgiveness and cleansing. Together these teach both the feeling of sin and the personal acceptance of grace the answer describes.

before.question: What is meant by "believing" the words "Given and shed for you for the forgiveness of sins"?
before.answer: Thereby is meant that we heartily feel our sin and unworthiness before God, but also that we confidently accept for ourselves the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ
before.right: To heartily feel our sin and unworthiness, and confidently accept God's grace in Christ

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 John 2:15 says that if anyone loves the world, "the love of the Father is not in him," which matches the printed answer.

before.question: According to 1 John 2:15, if anyone loves the world, what is not in him?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul says whoever eats unworthily is guilty against the Lord's body and blood, and each must examine himself, since eating without recognizing the body brings judgment. The answer's wording about not feeling or repenting sins and not believing follows from this.

before.question: Who partake of the Lord's Supper unworthily?
before.answer: They who do not feel nor repent their sins, and who do not from their heart believe in Jesus
before.right: They who do not feel nor repent their sins, and who do not from their heart believe in Jesus

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Corinthians 11:25 gives the command "do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me" and sets no fixed interval, so the answer's quoted words and its claim that no schedule is given both come from this verse.

before.question: How often should we partake of the Lord's Supper?
before.answer: Christ has not told us how often we should partake, but He has said, "do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me."
before.right: Christ has not told us how often, but said, "do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me."

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The command "do this, as often as you drink it" (1 Cor 11:25), the promise of the new covenant poured out for you (Luke 22:20), and the invitation to approach the throne of grace in our need (Heb 4:16) together match the answer.

before.question: What should move us to partake of the Lord's Supper often?
before.answer: First of all, the command and promise of our Lord and Savior; then, our own great need, which is the reason for our Father's tender invitation and promise of grace
before.right: The command and promise of our Lord; our great need, which is why God invites and promises grace

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul records Jesus commanding, "do this in remembrance of Me" (11:24), and says that eating the bread and drinking the cup proclaims the Lord's death (11:26).

before.question: What must we do when we receive the Lord's Supper?
before.answer: We must remember our Savior and His death
before.right: We must remember our Savior and His death

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Christ commands, "do this in remembrance of Me," and says that eating the bread and drinking the cup proclaims the Lord's death until He comes, so His death is to be kept in mind.

before.question: How should we remember Christ's death?
before.answer: We should earnestly fix our mind upon the suffering and death of Christ, so that we may be strengthened in faith and in love to Him, who loved us unto death
before.right: We should fix our mind upon Christ's suffering and death to strengthen faith and love

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 John 4:19 says we love because God first loved us, so our love answers His prior love toward us. Ephesians 2:4 likewise grounds it in God's great love and mercy.

before.question: Why must we love God?
before.answer: We must love God because of His goodness toward us
before.right: We must love God because of His goodness toward us

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Second Peter 1:21 says men spoke from God as the Holy Spirit carried them, and Ephesians 3:5 names the prophets and apostles as those who received God's revelation. The verses shown do not mention evangelists as writers.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The shown verses support prophets and apostles as the human writers, but none of them names evangelists as writers; Ephesians 4:11 lists evangelists only as a gift to the church.

before.question: Who wrote the Bible?
before.answer: The holy prophets, evangelists, and apostles wrote the Bible
before.right: The holy prophets, evangelists, and apostles wrote the Bible

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 John 5:3 says the love of God is that we keep His commandments, and John 14:15 says that loving Jesus means keeping His commandments. Keeping God's commands, a holy life, shows love for God.

before.question: Whereby is it seen that we love God?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 37:5 tells us to commit our way to the LORD and trust Him, and Jeremiah 17:7 praises the one whose confidence is in Him. The "loving father" image is not in these verses.

before.question: When do we trust in God above all things?
before.answer: We trust in God above all things when we have confidence in Him as in a loving father, and when we look to Him for every blessing, and put all our affairs into His hands
before.right: We trust God as a loving father and look to Him for every blessing

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Genesis 17:1 calls God "God Almighty," Exodus 33:11 says the LORD spoke to Moses as a man speaks to his friend, and 1 Corinthians 1:9 says God is faithful.

before.question: Why must we trust in God alone?
before.answer: Because He is our almighty and faithful Friend
before.right: Because He is our almighty and faithful Friend

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Hosea 12:5 gives God's names ("the LORD is His name of renown"). Isaiah 52:6 ties knowing His name to His speaking, and Jeremiah 16:21 to His power and might, so His name is made known through His Word and works.

before.question: What is meant by the "name" of God?
before.answer: The names given to Him in the Bible, and everything by which He makes Himself known, such as His Word and His works.
before.right: The names given to Him in the Bible, and all by which He makes Himself known, such as His Word and works

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:7 forbids taking the LORD's name in vain, and Leviticus 19:12 shows this as swearing falsely by His name and so profaning it. The answer's wording about thoughtless, mocking use is the catechism's gloss on that irreverence.

before.question: When is the name of God taken in vain?
before.answer: When it is used in a thoughtless and mocking manner and without devotion and reverence
before.right: When used in thoughtless, mocking manner without devotion and reverence

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Leviticus 24:15-16 forbids cursing God and blaspheming the LORD's name, but no shown verse defines cursing by God's name as calling down evil on oneself, a neighbor, or a created thing. That definition is church teaching drawn from the Second Commandment.

before.question: What is it to curse by the name of God?
before.answer: It is to call down evil upon ourselves, our neighbor, or any other created thing, by the name of God
before.right: It is to call down evil upon ourselves, our neighbor, or any other created thing, by the name of God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Deuteronomy 6:13 says to take oaths in God's name, and Leviticus 19:12 forbids swearing falsely by His name, so swearing by God's name means calling Him to witness to what is said.

before.question: What is it to swear by the name of God?
before.answer: It is to bear witness to anything by the holy name of God
before.right: It is to bear witness to anything by the holy name of God

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Leviticus 19:12 forbids swearing falsely by God's name, profaning it, which shows disregard for God. The judgment the perjurer brings on himself is not stated in the shown verses; Zechariah 5:4 would supply it.

before.question: Why is it a great sin to commit perjury?
before.answer: Because the perjurer shows open disregard for God and the salvation of his own soul, and frankly calls down the judgment of God upon himself
before.right: The perjurer shows disregard for God and his own salvation, and calls down God's judgment upon himself

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:7 forbids taking the LORD's name in vain. Acts 19:13 shows exorcists using the name of Jesus as a formula over people with evil spirits, which the text presents as misuse.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The verses do not use the word "conjure" or define it, and Acts 19:13 concerns evil spirits rather than diseases in general, so the answer's wording goes a step beyond the text.

before.question: What is it to conjure by the name of God?
before.answer: It is trying to cure diseases, or to practice any other kind of superstition, by the name of God or a passage from the Bible
before.right: Trying to cure diseases or practice superstition by invoking God's name or passages from the Bible

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Second Timothy 3:15-17 says the Holy Scriptures make one wise for salvation through faith in Christ and fully equip the man of God for every good work, which supports the answer's claim of Scripture's sufficiency.

before.question: Is the Bible then the only safe rule of our faith and duty?
before.answer: Yes; the Bible alone contains full information of the will of God concerning our salvation
before.right: Yes; the Bible alone contains full information of the will of God concerning our salvation

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Leviticus 19:12 forbids swearing falsely by God's name (perjury). Jeremiah 8:8 condemns false teaching that claims God's Law while distorting it. Psalm 78:36-37 shows deceiving God with the mouth while the heart is disloyal (hypocrisy).

before.question: How do we lie and deceive by the name of God?
before.answer: By perjury, false teaching, and hypocrisy
before.right: By perjury, false teaching, and hypocrisy

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:7 says the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain, which matches the answer's core. The verse does not specify "great" punishment or a split between time and eternity.

before.question: What must he expect who takes the name of God in vain?
before.answer: Great punishment, both in time and eternity; the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain
before.right: Great punishment, both in time and eternity; the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 50:15 bids us call on God in the day of trouble, Psalm 116:17 pairs thanksgiving with calling on His name, and 1 Chronicles 29:13 gives thanks and praise to His name.

before.question: How do we use the name of God properly?
before.answer: When we sincerely call upon the name of God in every time of need, and worship Him with prayer, praise, and thanksgiving
before.right: When we sincerely call upon God in need and worship with prayer, praise, thanksgiving

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses name the seventh-day Sabbath as Israel's rest. Matthew 28:1 places the women's visit to the tomb on the first day of the week, but does not call it a day of rest or say Christians keep it.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The shown passages do not say Christ arose on the first day or that Christians rest on Sunday; that Sunday is the Christian day of rest is church teaching beyond these verses.

before.question: Which day is the day of rest among Christians?
before.answer: Sunday, the first day of the week, on which Christ arose from the dead
before.right: Sunday, the first day of the week, when Christ arose

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:10 says the seventh day is a Sabbath on which no work is done, which supports the rest from daily labor. The clause about instruction in the fear of the Lord is not in the shown verses.

before.question: How should we keep the day of rest holy?
before.answer: We must rest from our daily labor, that the time may be used for our instruction in the fear of the Lord.
before.right: Rest from labor so time may be used for God's instruction

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The answer comes from Luther's explanation of the Third Commandment in the Small Catechism, not from the shown verses, which speak of Sabbath observance and rest but not of despising preaching or God's Word.

before.question: According to Luther's explanation of the Third Commandment, what must we not despise if we are to keep the day of rest holy?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath and argues that a son or ox that falls into a pit is pulled out at once, so mercy and urgent rescue are lawful. The verses say Sabbath, not Sunday.

before.question: According to the catechism, what work is permitted on Sunday?
before.answer: Any work of necessity that cannot be delayed, and any loving kindness we may show our neighbor who is in need
before.right: Necessary work and loving kindness to those in need

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 13:9 names the second-table commandments (adultery, murder, stealing, coveting) and says they are summed up in "Love your neighbor as yourself," so the second table's substance is love to the neighbor.

before.question: What is the substance of the second table?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 22:39 commands loving your neighbor "as yourself," which assumes self-love is proper. Romans 12:3 warns against thinking of yourself more highly than you ought, matching the caution about selfishness. "God has made us" is not stated in these verses.

before.question: May we love ourselves?
before.answer: Yes, for God has made us, but we must beware of selfishness
before.right: Yes, for God has made us, but we must beware of selfishness

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 16:26 asks what a man profits if he gains the world and forfeits his soul, so the soul is put above all else. Matthew 10:28 says the soul cannot be killed by men, supporting its immortality.

before.question: What should a man care for most of all?
before.answer: For his soul, the immortal part of himself
before.right: For his soul, the immortal part of himself

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Psalm 119:18 asks God to open the psalmist's eyes to see wonders in His law, which is looking to God for light first. Psalm 119:17 asks to live and keep His word, which is the aim of reading it.

before.question: How do we rightly use the Word of God?
before.answer: We must first look to God for the light of His Spirit, and then read with devotion and an earnest purpose to live according to the Word
before.right: Seek God's Spirit, read with devotion, and earnestly purpose to live according to the Word

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus answers "who is my neighbor?" by the parable: the one who showed mercy to the man in need, even a Samaritan to a Jew, is the neighbor. The verses show neighborliness reaching across group lines, though they do not state "every human being."

before.question: Who is our neighbor?
before.answer: Every human being is our neighbor.
before.right: Every human being is our neighbor.

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Jesus says "love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you," which answers "Yes." The clause that even an enemy is our neighbor is an inference, not stated in these verses.

before.question: Must we love also our enemies?
before.answer: Yes; for even our enemy is our neighbor
before.right: Yes; for even our enemy is our neighbor

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses give the command, a promise, and that obeying parents "is right" (Eph 6:1-3), but none says God placed parents over us to care for us. That reason is the catechism's own teaching.

before.question: Why must we honor father and mother?
before.answer: Because God has placed them over us to care for us
before.right: Because God has placed them over us to care for us

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Children are told to obey their parents, Ephesians 6:1 "in the Lord" and Colossians 3:20 "in everything." The verses teach obedience, not the wording about attitude or behavior when parents are absent.

before.question: How are children to show that they honor father and mother?
before.answer: By respectful, loving, and willing obedience and by good behavior to their parents, both in their presence and in their absence
before.right: By respectful, loving, and willing obedience and good behavior to parents, both in presence and absence

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Romans 13:1 says everyone must submit to governing authorities, which are appointed by God, and Ephesians 6:5 tells servants to obey their earthly masters. The verses name rulers and employers, not guardians or teachers, which the answer adds as examples.

before.question: Whom must we honor and obey besides our parents?
before.answer: All those whom God has placed over us, such as guardians, employers, teachers, and the government
before.right: All those God has placed over us: guardians, employers, teachers, government

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 6:4 and Proverbs 22:6 hold the duty to bring children up in the Lord's discipline and instruction and to train them in the right way. The shown verses do not clearly state the duties to love or to pray for children.

before.question: What is the duty of parents toward their children?
before.answer: They must love them, pray for them, bring them up in the fear of the Lord, and in everything seek their temporal and spiritual good
before.right: Love them, pray for them, bring them up in the fear of the Lord, and seek their good

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 6:3 states the promise directly: "that it may go well with you and that you may have a long life on the earth," which matches the answer's wording.

before.question: What is God's promise to those who honor father and mother?
before.answer: It shall be well with them, and they shall live long on the earth
before.right: It shall be well with them, and they shall live long on the earth

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Ephesians 6:2-3 gives the promise that it may go well with children who honor their parents and that they may have long life, so the blessing for obedient children follows from the text. The verses say nothing about nations, so that part of the answer is not drawn from them.

before.question: Is this promise yet effective?
before.answer: Yes; in this sense, that special blessings rest upon obedient children, and upon every nation honoring father and mother
before.right: Yes; in this sense, that special blessings rest upon obedient children, and upon every nation honoring father and mother

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Acts 17:26 says God determined the appointed times and boundaries of the lands of the nations, which supports God giving each people its land. The purpose clause about loving and helping it prosper is not in the verses.

before.question: Has God given us also a land?
before.answer: Yes; He has given us our native land, that we may love it and help it to prosper
before.right: He has given us our native land to love and help prosper

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The command to honor father and mother forbids the opposite, and Deuteronomy 27:16 condemns whoever dishonors them, which fits despising and giving offense to parents.

before.question: What does the fourth commandment forbid?
before.answer: To despise and give offense to father and mother
before.right: To despise and give offense to father and mother

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses do not say that God wills all people to use His Word. The answer is the catechism's teaching about Scripture, not a statement in these passages.

before.question: Who should read the Bible?
before.answer: It is the will of God that all should use His Word and love it as a dear gift
before.right: All should use His Word and love it as a dear gift

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:13 forbids murder, and taking a neighbor's life is murder. The wider phrase "bodily harm" is an extension of the commandment that Matthew 5:21-22 also reflects, though those verses are not shown as stating it.

before.question: How is the fifth commandment, "You shall not murder," transgressed in its most direct way?
before.answer: By taking our neighbor's life, or by doing him any bodily harm
before.right: By taking our neighbor's life, or by doing him any bodily harm

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 18:6-7 warns that whoever causes a believing little one to stumble, and the one through whom such stumbling blocks come, faces woe. Causing another to sin is the answer given.

before.question: Can we kill also our neighbor's soul?
before.answer: Yes; when we cause him to sin, either by purposely leading him astray, or by bad example, thus helping to destroy his soul
before.right: Yes; by purposely leading him astray or by bad example that destroys his soul

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Deuteronomy 32:39 says God alone brings death and gives life, and Job 12:10 says every living thing's life is in His hand. Self-killing is ruled out by inference, since no verse names it directly.

before.question: May we take our own life?
before.answer: No; God has given us life, and He alone has the right to take it
before.right: No; God has given us life, and He alone has the right to take it

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: God Himself makes the woman, brings her to the man, and states the pattern of leaving parents and becoming one flesh, in the garden. Christ later confirms this in Matthew 19:6.

before.question: Who has instituted marriage?
before.answer: God Himself instituted it in Paradise
before.right: God Himself instituted it in Paradise

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: 1 Corinthians 6:18 says that he who sins sexually sins against his own body, which matches the printed answer.

before.question: According to 1 Corinthians 6:18, against what does the person who commits sexual immorality sin?

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Matthew 26:41 says to "watch and pray" so as not to enter temptation; 2 Corinthians 7:1 says to cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit.

before.question: How can we be kept pure?
before.answer: We must watch and pray, and avoid everything that awakens impure desires
before.right: We must watch and pray, and avoid everything that awakens impure desires

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: The shown verses warn against drunkenness, carousing, and obscenity or crude joking, but none says these or bad company, amusements, or books awaken impure desires. The full list is catechetical application.

before.question: What things awaken impure desires?
before.answer: Gluttony and drunkenness, immoral and exciting amusements, bad company, the reading of improper books, and everything that excites carnal and impure thoughts
before.right: Gluttony, drunkenness, immoral amusements, bad company, improper books, and all that excites carnal thoughts

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Drunkenness is named among works whose practitioners will not inherit God's kingdom (Gal 5:21; 1 Cor 6:10). Gluttony is warned against for bringing poverty and ruin (Prov 23:20-21).
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The answer says gluttony shuts one out of the kingdom, but the shown verses name only drunkenness as excluding; gluttony is warned against only for bringing poverty and ruin.

before.question: Are not gluttony and drunkenness also dangerous sins?
before.answer: Yes, indeed; they are a shameful abuse of God's gifts, by which we ruin soul and body and shut ourselves out from the kingdom of God
before.right: Yes; they shamefully abuse God's gifts and ruin soul and body, excluding us from His kingdom

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:14 only forbids adultery. The answer's wider duties come from 1 Thessalonians 4:3-4 (abstain from sexual immorality, control your body in holiness), Hebrews 13:4 (honor marriage, keep the bed undefiled), and Ephesians 5:25 (husbands love wives).

before.question: What does God require of us in the sixth commandment?
before.answer: We must live a chaste and pure life, whether we are married or unmarried, husband and wife loving and honoring each other
before.right: Live chaste and pure whether married or unmarried, with husband and wife loving and honoring each other

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 24:27 says Jesus explained what all the Scriptures wrote about Himself, and John 5:39 says they testify about Him so that people may have eternal life by coming to Him.

before.question: What is the substance of all the books of the Bible?
before.answer: The great truth that Jesus is the way to salvation for all who believe
before.right: The great truth that Jesus is the way to salvation for all who believe

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:15 forbids stealing, and Exodus 22:7 describes goods taken from a neighbor's house without consent. The "smallest part" wording is Luther's gloss and is not stated in these verses.

before.question: What is it to steal?
before.answer: To steal is to take from our neighbor even the smallest part of his property against his will
before.right: To take from our neighbor even the smallest part of his property against his will

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: No shown verse divides theft into coarse and artful kinds. The shown passages describe thieves breaking in by night, robbers plundering, and a thief stealing for hunger, but the coarse/artful distinction comes from the catechism's explanation of the Eighth Commandment.

before.question: How is stealing done?
before.answer: In a coarse or in an artful manner
before.right: In a coarse or in an artful manner

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:15 forbids stealing, and Exodus 22:8 speaks of taking a neighbor's property. The "coarse" label and "without any right" wording are the catechism's own sorting of theft, not stated in these verses.

before.question: Who steal in a coarse manner?
before.answer: Those who, without any right or permission whatever, take their neighbor's money or property
before.right: Those who take their neighbor's money or property without any right or permission

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Leviticus 19:13 forbids defrauding a neighbor or robbing him, and withholding a hired hand's wages overnight, which matches taking or withholding another's property by fraud.

before.question: Who steal in an artful manner?
before.answer: Those who take or withhold the property of others by any kind of fraud
before.right: Those who take or withhold the property of others by any kind of fraud

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Proverbs 29:24 says a partner to a thief hates his own soul, and Psalm 50:18 condemns one who befriends a thief and throws in his lot with him. Together they teach that such partnership is wrong.
gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.doubt: The verses do not literally say the partner is "no better than the thief"; that comparison is a reasonable inference from Psalm 50:18 placing him alongside the thief and adulterers.

before.question: Is it wrong to be a partner with a thief?
before.answer: Yes; the partner of a thief is no better than the thief
before.right: Yes; the partner of a thief is no better than the thief

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Paul calls believers stewards who must be found faithful (1 Cor 4:1-2), and Luke 16:2 shows a manager required to turn in an account of his management. Together they teach that we hold possessions as stewards and must answer for them.

before.question: May we not do with our property what we please?
before.answer: No; we are but keepers of God's gifts, and we must once give an account of how we have used them
before.right: No; we are but keepers of God's gifts, and we must give an account of how we have used them

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:16 forbids bearing false witness against a neighbor. Exodus 23:1-2 covers a false report spread outside court and false testimony in a lawsuit, so the answer follows from these verses.

before.question: What is "false witness"?
before.answer: All untruthful speaking about our neighbor, in or out of court
before.right: All untruthful speaking about our neighbor, in or out of court

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Proverbs 17:15 calls acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous detestable, matching the judge clause. Deuteronomy 19:16 describes a false witness testifying in court to accuse someone of a crime, matching the witness clause.

before.question: How does one bear false witness in court?
before.answer: When a witness swears to a lie, and when a judge decides wrong to be right, and right to be wrong
before.right: When a witness swears to a lie, and when a judge decides wrong to be right, and right to be wrong

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:16 forbids bearing false witness against a neighbor, which covers lies about him; Leviticus 19:16 forbids spreading slander among the people, which covers slander and defamation.

before.question: How do we bear false witness out of court?
before.answer: When we tell lies about our neighbor and slander or defame him in our conversation
before.right: When we tell lies about our neighbor and slander or defame him in our conversation

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Luke 16:16 sets "the Law and the Prophets" against "the gospel of the kingdom of God," showing Scripture's teaching as Law and Gospel. The answer is taught by that contrast rather than stated as a formal division.

before.question: How is the Bible divided in regard to its teaching?
before.answer: It is divided into Law and Gospel
before.right: It is divided into Law and Gospel

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:16 forbids false witness against a neighbor, and Ephesians 4:25 bids us put off falsehood and speak truthfully to our neighbor. The duties to excuse him and read his acts charitably are not stated in these verses.

before.question: What does God require of us in the eighth commandment?
before.answer: We must always be truthful, excuse, and speak well of our neighbor, as far as truth permits, and look upon all his acts as well-meant
before.right: Always be truthful, excuse, and speak well of neighbor as truth permits, viewing acts well-meant

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:17 forbids coveting a neighbor's house, wife, servants, animals, or anything that belongs to him, which is the sinful desire the answer describes.

before.question: What do the ninth and tenth commandments forbid?
before.answer: All sinful desire to get what belongs to our neighbor
before.right: All sinful desire to get what belongs to our neighbor

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: God's law commands holiness ("Be holy because I am holy"), and 2 Corinthians 7:1 calls for cleansing from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness. The thoughts and words detail is only implied.

before.question: What, then, does God require of us in His holy Law?
before.answer: Perfect purity and holiness in all our thoughts and desires, words and acts
before.right: Perfect purity and holiness in all our thoughts and desires, words and acts

gutenberg-sunday-school-question-books:p.note: Exodus 20:5-6 states it directly: God is a jealous God, visiting iniquity on those who hate Him, and showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Him and keep His commandments.

before.question: What does God say at the end of the commandments about those who hate him and those who love him?
